types.name: TokenEntitlements

TokenEntitlements holds compressed C2S entitlements embedded in user tokens.
 OPA returns this structure directly; the token authority embeds it in the JWT service_entitlements claim.
 grants may contain exact or wildcard grant tokens; generated helpers normalize them before authorization.

fields.name: grants
fields.description: grants is a flat list of generated grant tokens, e.g. PACKAGE_SERVICE_RPC.

fields.name: data_grants
fields.description:
data_grants is a flat list of generated data-entitlement grant tokens, e.g.
 PACKAGE_RECORD_FIELD. A data grant names what the caller may SEE RAW: a MAY_*
 redact field with a matching grant egresses raw; absent a grant the field gets
 its most-protective default (MAY_REDACT -> REDACT, MAY_ANONYMIZE -> ANONYMIZE).
 Stamped by OPA at token-exchange time alongside grants — an identity property,
 never a request parameter.

fields.name: principal_scope
fields.description:
principal_scope is how wide the caller's authority over PRINCIPALS is, as a
 spec.PrincipalScope enum VALUE NAME (e.g. "PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_ANY"). It is the
 claim the generated (spec.owner_default) guard reads to tell an owner acting
 on its own row from a principal whose authority is wider than itself.
 Absent, empty, PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_UNSPECIFIED and PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_SELF_ONLY all
 mean self-scoped: the guard fails closed, so a policy that stamps nothing
 leaves every caller exactly as narrow as it is today.
 Stamped by OPA at token-exchange time alongside grants — an identity
 property, never a request parameter.

fields.name: azp
fields.description:
azp restricts these entitlements to tokens with a matching authorized party.
 Empty = entitlements apply regardless of azp.

fields.name: logger
fields.description: logger configures kmaker process logging.

message.name: LoggerConfig
message.description:
LoggerConfig represents the configuration for a logger instance.
 It controls the output format, verbosity level, and formatting options.

 Example usage:
   - Development mode with console output and pretty printing for local debugging
   - Production mode with JSON output and no pretty printing for log aggregation

fields.name: name
fields.description: Name is the logger name/component identifier

fields.name: format
fields.description:
Format determines the output format for log messages (JSON or console)
 Default: FORMAT_JSON in production, FORMAT_CONSOLE in development

enum_values.name: FORMAT_JSON
enum_values.description: FORMAT_JSON outputs logs as JSON objects, ideal for structured logging and log aggregation systems

enum_values.name: FORMAT_CONSOLE
enum_values.description: FORMAT_CONSOLE outputs logs in a human-readable console format, ideal for development and debugging

fields.name: level
fields.description:
Level sets the minimum severity level for log messages to be output
 Messages below this level will be filtered out
 Default: LEVEL_INFO in production, LEVEL_DEBUG in development

enum_values.name: LEVEL_TRACE
enum_values.description: LEVEL_TRACE is the most verbose log level, used for detailed debugging information

enum_values.name: LEVEL_DEBUG
enum_values.description: LEVEL_DEBUG is used for debugging information, less verbose than trace

enum_values.name: LEVEL_INFO
enum_values.description: LEVEL_INFO is used for informational messages about normal operations

enum_values.name: LEVEL_WARN
enum_values.description: LEVEL_WARN is used for warning messages about potentially problematic situations

enum_values.name: LEVEL_ERROR
enum_values.description: LEVEL_ERROR is used for error messages about failures and problems

fields.name: development
fields.description:
Development enables development mode which:
   - Uses console format by default
   - Enables stack traces for warnings and errors
   - Uses more human-readable timestamps
 Default: false (production mode)

fields.name: pretty_print
fields.description:
PrettyPrint enables pretty-printed output for JSON format
 This makes JSON logs more readable but increases output size
 Should be disabled in production for performance
 Default: false

fields.name: output_paths
fields.description:
OutputPaths is a list of file paths or URLs to write logs to
 Use "stdout" or "stderr" for console output
 Example: ["stdout", "/var/log/app.log"]
constraints: must be a valid file path (type: PATH_ANY)

fields.name: error_output_paths
fields.description:
ErrorOutputPaths is a list of file paths or URLs to write error logs to
 Use "stderr" for console error output
 Example: ["stderr", "/var/log/app-errors.log"]
constraints: must be a valid file path (type: PATH_ANY)

fields.name: disable_caller
fields.description:
DisableCaller disables automatic inclusion of caller information (file:line) in log entries
 Default: false (caller information is included)

fields.name: disable_stacktrace
fields.description:
DisableStacktrace disables automatic stacktraces for error-level and above log entries
 Default: false (stacktraces are included for errors)

fields.name: initial_fields
cluster_ca
fields.description: cluster_ca holds trust anchors that kernel nodes should trust.

message.name: X509Cert
message.description:
ProtoCert represents an X.509 certificate.
 The certificate is stored as a base64-encoded PEM block.
 Use NewProtoCert() in Go with DER-encoded certificate bytes to create.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is a unique identifier for the certificate

fields.name: base64
fields.description: Base64 contains the base64url-encoded PEM certificate block

fields.name: signing_ca
fields.description:
signing_ca is the cluster signing CA used to issue kernel certificates.
 The private key is present in the mounted kmaker config and must be backed
 by a Kubernetes Secret owned by operator.

message.name: X509CertChain
message.description:
X509CertChain contains a certificate chain and optional private key.
 chain[0] is the leaf (end-entity) cert, followed by intermediates, ordered toward root.
 When key is present, the chain is a full credential suitable for TLS.

fields.name: chain
fields.description: chain[0] is the leaf (end-entity) cert, followed by intermediates, ordered toward root.

fields.name: key
fields.description: optional private key for the leaf cert; present when chain is a full credential.

message.name: Key
message.description: Key represents a private cryptographic key (alias for ProtoKey).

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is a unique identifier for the key (corresponds to kid in JWK)

fields.name: base64
fields.description: Base64 contains the base64url-encoded PEM private key block

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created
 Valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is an optional stable key for chain collections.

fields.name: spiffe_prefix
fields.description:
spiffe_prefix is the SPIFFE trust domain for kernel SPIFFE URI SANs: the
 URI authority, so it must not contain '/'. Certificates minted here
 receive spiffe://<spiffe_prefix>/kernel. Operator supplies this from
 operator.Config.spiffe_prefix.

fields.name: token_audience
fields.description: token_audience is the required Kubernetes TokenReview audience.

fields.name: kernel_service_accounts
fields.description:
kernel_service_accounts are Kubernetes service accounts allowed to request
 kernel certificates. Empty means namespace=schematic, name=kernel.

fields.name: kernel_cert_lifetime_seconds
fields.description: kernel_cert_lifetime_seconds caps issued kernel certificate lifetimes.

fields.name: tls
fields.description:
tls is the optional serving certificate for kmaker's own gRPC listener.
 When unset, kmaker starts without transport TLS for local/dev only.

fields.name: health_probe_port
fields.description:
health_probe_port is the plaintext gRPC port for k8s health probes.
 Kmaker's hand-written bootstrap bypasses the generated ServiceManager,
 so this field must be on Kmaker.Config (not only on Grpcconfig.Config).
 Default matches the platform-wide health probe port.

 It contains the public key parameters for RSA (e, n), EC (crv, x, y), or OKP (crv, x) keys.
 JWK is used for key distribution and verification in JSON-based protocols like JWT.

fields.name: kty
fields.description: Kty is the key type parameter (RSA, EC, or OKP)

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_RSA
enum_values.description: KeyTypeRsa represents an RSA key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_EC
enum_values.description: KeyTypeEc represents an Elliptic Curve key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_OKP
enum_values.description: KeyTypeOkp represents an Octet Key Pair (EdDSA) key type

fields.name: alg
fields.description: Alg is the algorithm intended for use with the key (e.g., "RS384", "ES256", "EdDSA")

fields.name: kid
fields.description: Kid is the key ID used to match keys with signatures

fields.name: use
fields.description: Use indicates the intended use of the key (sig for signatures, enc for encryption)

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_SIG
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeSig indicates the key is used for digital signatures

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_ENC
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeEnc indicates the key is used for encryption

fields.name: e
fields.description: E is the RSA public exponent (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: n
fields.description: N is the RSA modulus (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: crv
fields.description: Crv is the elliptic curve name (e.g., P-256, P-384, P-521, Ed25519)

fields.name: x
fields.description: X is the x coordinate for EC keys or the public key for OKP (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: y
fields.description: Y is the y coordinate for EC keys (base64url encoded without padding, not used for OKP)

fields.name: exp
fields.description:
Exp is the expiration in epoch seconds. This is not part of the JWK spec as the spec does
 not specify how to handle public key expiration.
 When stored in a collection with epoch_expiration, the state store computes TTL = exp - now
 and auto-evicts the entry on expiry.

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created (optional).
 If set, valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

types.name: ArchiveConfig
types.description:
ArchiveConfig configures shipping the redo log to an object store. Writes
 are acknowledged locally; shipping is asynchronous and never blocks an
 append. Credentials are the workload's ambient identity (Google Cloud
 Application Default Credentials), never a key in this config.

fields.name: gcs_bucket
fields.description: gcs_bucket is the Google Cloud Storage bucket the archive is written to.

fields.name: prefix
fields.description:
prefix namespaces the archive inside the bucket. Each writer's objects
 live under <prefix>/<member>/<store>/, so several members ship
 independently.

fields.name: checkpoint_interval_seconds
fields.description:
checkpoint_interval_seconds is how often a full checkpoint (the complete
 store state, recording the redo position it covers) is shipped. A restore
 loads the newest checkpoint and replays the segments shipped after it.

fields.name: segment_interval_seconds
fields.description:
segment_interval_seconds is how often the active redo log is rotated and
 shipped as a segment without folding a baseline: the cost is the writes
 since the last rotation, not the store. It is the recovery point after
 losing the volume. 0 (the default) turns rotation off, and the recovery
 point is then one roll_interval_seconds.

 automates the redo-log lifecycle (UC2) for service_store-annotated types.
 It is embedded in the ServiceManager config.

fields.name: roll_interval_seconds

 per-node deterministic roll offset (hash(node-id) % roll_interval).

Compression selects at-rest compression for rolled/archived files and
 snapshot baselines. The live redo-log append tail is always uncompressed so

enums.name: EntitlementLevel
enums.description:
EntitlementLevel is the data-entitlement decision for one MAY_* field. The rule
 is FAIL-CLOSED: absent an explicit decision (UNSPECIFIED = 0, the proto3
 default), the field gets its MOST-PROTECTIVE level — MAY_REDACT defaults to
 REDACT, MAY_ANONYMIZE defaults to ANONYMIZE. A grant in the caller's token
 loosens a field toward RAW; it can never loosen below a hard floor
 (DROP/PSEUDONYMIZE fields are caller-independent and always applied).

values.name: ENTITLEMENT_LEVEL_UNSPECIFIED
values.description: No decision recorded — the field gets its most-protective default.

values.name: ENTITLEMENT_LEVEL_ANONYMIZE
values.description:
Replace with a keyed HMAC surrogate. Valid only on string/bytes fields; on any
 other field the generated transform clamps ANONYMIZE up to REDACT.

values.name: ENTITLEMENT_LEVEL_REDACT
values.description: Clear the field to its zero value (a message field clears the whole subtree).

values.name: ENTITLEMENT_LEVEL_RAW
values.description:
Egress the field raw — the explicit loosening grant ("this caller is
 permitted to see the value"). Only ever set from a matching token data grant.

types.name: Config
types.description:
Config is the single configuration type for all services.

 Bootstrap fields (endpoints, instance_id, private_key, trusted_cas) are loaded
 from YAML at boot and used to connect to the cluster.

 Runtime fields (ping_interval_ms, rebalance_interval_ms, listen_address,
 max_request_size, request_timeout_seconds, logger, shutdown_timeout_seconds)
 are delivered by the cluster via ServiceConfigState and can change at any time.

 TLS certificates are obtained automatically by the servicemanager via X509Mint
 after token exchange — they are not part of the config.

fields.name: endpoints
fields.description:
Cluster endpoints. Set in bootstrap file; can be updated at runtime
 via ServiceConfigState to add/remove endpoints dynamically.

message.name: Host
message.description:
Host identifies a network endpoint by hostname/IP and port.
 The host field accepts either an FQDN or an IP address (v4/v6).

fields.name: host
fields.description: Hostname or IP address (e.g. "api.example.com" or "10.0.0.1").
constraints: must be a valid hostname or IP address

fields.name: port
fields.description: Port number (1-65535).
constraints: must be a valid network port (1-65535)

fields.name: protocol
fields.description: Transport protocol. Default TCP (zero value).

fields.name: instance_id
fields.description:
instance_id uniquely identifies this running instance/replica.
 Used for leader elections on boundaries with (spec.leader) = true.
 If empty, a random ID is generated at client creation time.

fields.name: private_key
fields.description:
private_key is used to mint throwaway bootstrap JWTs for the
 token exchange flow. The kid is in private_key.id;
 identity (subject/audience) comes from the delegate looked up
 by TokenExchanger using the matching kid.
 If absent, cloud-native authentication is attempted.

message.name: Key
message.description: Key represents a private cryptographic key (alias for ProtoKey).

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is a unique identifier for the key (corresponds to kid in JWK)

fields.name: base64
fields.description: Base64 contains the base64url-encoded PEM private key block

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created
 Valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

fields.name: ping_interval_ms
fields.description:
ping_interval_ms controls how often each endpoint is pinged for latency measurement.
 Default: 5000 (5 seconds)

fields.name: rebalance_interval_ms
fields.description:
rebalance_interval_ms controls how often the active connection is re-evaluated
 based on latency. Default: 10000 (10 seconds)

fields.name: listen_address
fields.description: listen_address is the bind address for the gRPC server. Default port 8443.

fields.name: max_request_size
fields.description:
max_request_size is the maximum request size in bytes.
 Must be greater than 0. Default: 10MB (10485760 bytes)

fields.name: request_timeout_seconds
fields.description:
request_timeout_seconds is the timeout for client requests.
 Must be positive. Default: 30 seconds.

fields.name: logger
fields.description:
logger configures the logger for the service.
 Controls log format (JSON/console), level, output paths, and more.

message.name: LoggerConfig
message.description:
LoggerConfig represents the configuration for a logger instance.
 It controls the output format, verbosity level, and formatting options.

 Example usage:
   - Development mode with console output and pretty printing for local debugging
   - Production mode with JSON output and no pretty printing for log aggregation

fields.name: name
fields.description: Name is the logger name/component identifier

fields.name: format
fields.description:
Format determines the output format for log messages (JSON or console)
 Default: FORMAT_JSON in production, FORMAT_CONSOLE in development

enum_values.name: FORMAT_JSON
enum_values.description: FORMAT_JSON outputs logs as JSON objects, ideal for structured logging and log aggregation systems

enum_values.name: FORMAT_CONSOLE
enum_values.description: FORMAT_CONSOLE outputs logs in a human-readable console format, ideal for development and debugging

fields.name: level
fields.description:
Level sets the minimum severity level for log messages to be output
 Messages below this level will be filtered out
 Default: LEVEL_INFO in production, LEVEL_DEBUG in development

enum_values.name: LEVEL_TRACE
enum_values.description: LEVEL_TRACE is the most verbose log level, used for detailed debugging information

enum_values.name: LEVEL_DEBUG
enum_values.description: LEVEL_DEBUG is used for debugging information, less verbose than trace

enum_values.name: LEVEL_INFO
enum_values.description: LEVEL_INFO is used for informational messages about normal operations

enum_values.name: LEVEL_WARN
enum_values.description: LEVEL_WARN is used for warning messages about potentially problematic situations

enum_values.name: LEVEL_ERROR
enum_values.description: LEVEL_ERROR is used for error messages about failures and problems

fields.name: development
fields.description:
Development enables development mode which:
   - Uses console format by default
   - Enables stack traces for warnings and errors
   - Uses more human-readable timestamps
 Default: false (production mode)

fields.name: pretty_print
fields.description:
PrettyPrint enables pretty-printed output for JSON format
 This makes JSON logs more readable but increases output size
 Should be disabled in production for performance
 Default: false

fields.name: output_paths
fields.description:
OutputPaths is a list of file paths or URLs to write logs to
 Use "stdout" or "stderr" for console output
 Example: ["stdout", "/var/log/app.log"]
constraints: must be a valid file path (type: PATH_ANY)

fields.name: error_output_paths
fields.description:
ErrorOutputPaths is a list of file paths or URLs to write error logs to
 Use "stderr" for console error output
 Example: ["stderr", "/var/log/app-errors.log"]
constraints: must be a valid file path (type: PATH_ANY)

fields.name: disable_caller
fields.description:
DisableCaller disables automatic inclusion of caller information (file:line) in log entries
 Default: false (caller information is included)

fields.name: disable_stacktrace
fields.description:
DisableStacktrace disables automatic stacktraces for error-level and above log entries
 Default: false (stacktraces are included for errors)

shutdown_timeout_seconds
fields.description:
shutdown_timeout_seconds is the maximum time (in seconds) to wait for graceful
 shutdown after SIGTERM before forcing immediate shutdown.
 Must be positive. Default: 30 seconds.

fields.name: max_concurrent_streams
fields.description:
max_concurrent_streams limits the number of concurrent gRPC streams per connection.
 Prevents resource exhaustion from clients opening unlimited streams.
 Default: 100. Set to 0 to use the gRPC library default (unlimited).

fields.name: max_send_msg_size
fields.description:
max_send_msg_size is the maximum response message size in bytes.
 Prevents the server from sending responses that could OOM clients.
 Default: 16MB (16777216 bytes). Set to 0 to use the gRPC library default.

fields.name: keepalive_min_time_seconds
fields.description:
keepalive_min_time_seconds is the minimum interval clients must wait between
 keepalive pings. Clients pinging more frequently are disconnected.
 Default: 30 seconds. Set to 0 to disable enforcement.

fields.name: trusted_cas
fields.description:
trusted_cas is the explicit list of CA certificates trusted for SPIFFE TLS
 verification when connecting to cluster endpoints. It must not be empty.

message.name: X509Cert
message.description:
ProtoCert represents an X.509 certificate.
 The certificate is stored as a base64-encoded PEM block.
 Use NewProtoCert() in Go with DER-encoded certificate bytes to create.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is a unique identifier for the certificate

fields.name: base64
fields.description: Base64 contains the base64url-encoded PEM certificate block

fields.name: spiffe_trust_domain
fields.description:
spiffe_trust_domain is the SPIFFE URI authority: a globally unique instance
 name for this autonomous-system instance (need not be a DNS domain).
 It must not contain '/', a scheme, query, or fragment, and carries no path.
 Service identity is built by the generated sys/spiffe helper as:
   spiffe://<spiffe_trust_domain>/system/<location_path...>/services/<service_label>
 If empty, SPIFFE IDs are not set on health reports or X509 URI SANs.

fields.name: location_path
fields.description:
location_path is this service instance's topology path under /system —
 opaque, tag-delimited, slash-separated segments, arity not fixed
 (e.g. "aws/123456789012/us-east-1a/cluster-7/team-a"). Segments follow the
 SPIFFE segment grammar and must not be reserved tags. Supplied by the
 operator/deployment from runtime config (where the service runs); it is
 not a token claim. May be empty (no topology tiers).

fields.name: disk_persistence

 ServiceManager-owned redo-log lifecycle for generated service_store stores.
 When present at ServiceManager creation, the generated ServiceManager opens
 the per-store redo logs, exposes those handles to service code, and owns
 scheduled compaction/roll. It is not hot-reloaded; when absent, typed
 diskstore helpers remain available but no managed roll loop is started.

fields.name: anonymize_hmac_key
fields.description:
anonymize_hmac_key is the per-deployment data-entitlement ANONYMIZE secret:
 the keyed-HMAC key the generated service wrapper supplies to Sanitize<T> so
 a value pseudonymizes to the same surrogate at any depth, across services
 and restarts. Required only by services whose records carry
 ANONYMIZE-capable (spec.redact) fields — the generated pseudonymize
 primitives fail loud on an empty key.

fields.name: health_probe_port
fields.description:
health_probe_port is the port for a separate PLAINTEXT gRPC listener that
 serves ONLY grpc.health.v1. k8s kubelet probes are plaintext-only and
 cannot speak TLS, so the main TLS port (listen_address) is invisible to
 them. This listener runs on a completely separate grpc.Server / tonic
 Server / NettyServerBuilder with no TLS, no auth interceptors, and no
 business services registered — isolation is the security argument.
 The health status reflects the same StatusSink-driven state as the TLS
 health endpoint: NOT_SERVING until bootstrap completes, then tracks
 handler health (UNHEALTHY → NOT_SERVING, recovery → SERVING).
 Default: 8444. Set to 0 to disable the plaintext health probe listener.

fields.name: config_fetch_timeout_seconds
fields.description:
config_fetch_timeout_seconds bounds the generated state-singleton startup
 fetch. A singleton Get can race the state authority's own convergence and
 return a value that has not been fully seeded yet; the generated fetch()
 retries with the watch-restart backoff for as long as the fetched value
 fails its own generated validate<T>, and fails loudly once this budget is
 spent rather than handing the caller a value it already knows is invalid.
 Must be positive. Default: 30 seconds.

message.name: Host
message.description:
Host identifies a network endpoint by hostname/IP and port.
 The host field accepts either an FQDN or an IP address (v4/v6).

fields.name: host
fields.description: Hostname or IP address (e.g. "api.example.com" or "10.0.0.1").
constraints: must be a valid hostname or IP address

fields.name: port
fields.description: Port number (1-65535).
constraints: must be a valid network port (1-65535)

fields.name: protocol
fields.description: Transport protocol. Default TCP (zero value).

fields.name: instance_id
fields.description:
instance_id uniquely identifies this running instance/replica.
 Used for leader elections on boundaries with (spec.leader) = true.
 If empty, a random ID is generated at client creation time.

fields.name: private_key
fields.description:
private_key is used to mint throwaway bootstrap JWTs for the
 token exchange flow. The kid is in private_key.id;
 identity (subject/audience) comes from the delegate looked up
 by TokenExchanger using the matching kid.
 If absent, cloud-native authentication is attempted.

message.name: Key
message.description: Key represents a private cryptographic key (alias for ProtoKey).

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is a unique identifier for the key (corresponds to kid in JWK)

fields.name: base64
fields.description: Base64 contains the base64url-encoded PEM private key block

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created
 Valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

fields.name: ping_interval_ms
fields.description:
ping_interval_ms controls how often each endpoint is pinged for latency measurement.
 Default: 5000 (5 seconds)

fields.name: rebalance_interval_ms
fields.description:
rebalance_interval_ms controls how often the active connection is re-evaluated
 based on latency. Default: 10000 (10 seconds)

fields.name: listen_address
fields.description: listen_address is the bind address for the gRPC server. Default port 8443.

fields.name: max_request_size
fields.description:
max_request_size is the maximum request size in bytes.
 Must be greater than 0. Default: 10MB (10485760 bytes)

fields.name: request_timeout_seconds
fields.description:
request_timeout_seconds is the timeout for client requests.
 Must be positive. Default: 30 seconds.

fields.name: logger
fields.description:
logger configures the logger for the service.
 Controls log format (JSON/console), level, output paths, and more.

message.name: LoggerConfig
message.description:
LoggerConfig represents the configuration for a logger instance.
 It controls the output format, verbosity level, and formatting options.

 Example usage:
   - Development mode with console output and pretty printing for local debugging
   - Production mode with JSON output and no pretty printing for log aggregation

fields.name: name
fields.description: Name is the logger name/component identifier

fields.name: format
fields.description:
Format determines the output format for log messages (JSON or console)
 Default: FORMAT_JSON in production, FORMAT_CONSOLE in development

enum_values.name: FORMAT_JSON
enum_values.description: FORMAT_JSON outputs logs as JSON objects, ideal for structured logging and log aggregation systems

enum_values.name: FORMAT_CONSOLE
enum_values.description: FORMAT_CONSOLE outputs logs in a human-readable console format, ideal for development and debugging

fields.name: level
fields.description:
Level sets the minimum severity level for log messages to be output
 Messages below this level will be filtered out
 Default: LEVEL_INFO in production, LEVEL_DEBUG in development

enum_values.name: LEVEL_TRACE
enum_values.description: LEVEL_TRACE is the most verbose log level, used for detailed debugging information

enum_values.name: LEVEL_DEBUG
enum_values.description: LEVEL_DEBUG is used for debugging information, less verbose than trace

enum_values.name: LEVEL_INFO
enum_values.description: LEVEL_INFO is used for informational messages about normal operations

enum_values.name: LEVEL_WARN
enum_values.description: LEVEL_WARN is used for warning messages about potentially problematic situations

enum_values.name: LEVEL_ERROR
enum_values.description: LEVEL_ERROR is used for error messages about failures and problems

fields.name: development
fields.description:
Development enables development mode which:
   - Uses console format by default
   - Enables stack traces for warnings and errors
   - Uses more human-readable timestamps
 Default: false (production mode)

fields.name: pretty_print
fields.description:
PrettyPrint enables pretty-printed output for JSON format
 This makes JSON logs more readable but increases output size
 Should be disabled in production for performance
 Default: false

fields.name: output_paths
fields.description:
OutputPaths is a list of file paths or URLs to write logs to
 Use "stdout" or "stderr" for console output
 Example: ["stdout", "/var/log/app.log"]
constraints: must be a valid file path (type: PATH_ANY)

fields.name: error_output_paths
fields.description:
ErrorOutputPaths is a list of file paths or URLs to write error logs to
 Use "stderr" for console error output
 Example: ["stderr", "/var/log/app-errors.log"]
constraints: must be a valid file path (type: PATH_ANY)

fields.name: disable_caller
fields.description:
DisableCaller disables automatic inclusion of caller information (file:line) in log entries
 Default: false (caller information is included)

fields.name: disable_stacktrace
fields.description:
DisableStacktrace disables automatic stacktraces for error-level and above log entries
 Default: false (stacktraces are included for errors)

fields.name: initial_fields
shutdown_timeout_seconds
fields.description:
shutdown_timeout_seconds is the maximum time (in seconds) to wait for graceful
 shutdown after SIGTERM before forcing immediate shutdown.
 Must be positive. Default: 30 seconds.

fields.name: max_concurrent_streams
fields.description:
max_concurrent_streams limits the number of concurrent gRPC streams per connection.
 Prevents resource exhaustion from clients opening unlimited streams.
 Default: 100. Set to 0 to use the gRPC library default (unlimited).

fields.name: max_send_msg_size
fields.description:
max_send_msg_size is the maximum response message size in bytes.
 Prevents the server from sending responses that could OOM clients.
 Default: 16MB (16777216 bytes). Set to 0 to use the gRPC library default.

fields.name: keepalive_min_time_seconds
fields.description:
keepalive_min_time_seconds is the minimum interval clients must wait between
 keepalive pings. Clients pinging more frequently are disconnected.
 Default: 30 seconds. Set to 0 to disable enforcement.

fields.name: trusted_cas
fields.description:
trusted_cas is the explicit list of CA certificates trusted for SPIFFE TLS
 verification when connecting to cluster endpoints. It must not be empty.

message.name: X509Cert
message.description:
ProtoCert represents an X.509 certificate.
 The certificate is stored as a base64-encoded PEM block.
 Use NewProtoCert() in Go with DER-encoded certificate bytes to create.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is a unique identifier for the certificate

fields.name: base64
fields.description: Base64 contains the base64url-encoded PEM certificate block

fields.name: spiffe_trust_domain
fields.description:
spiffe_trust_domain is the SPIFFE URI authority: a globally unique instance
 name for this autonomous-system instance (need not be a DNS domain).
 It must not contain '/', a scheme, query, or fragment, and carries no path.
 Service identity is built by the generated sys/spiffe helper as:
   spiffe://<spiffe_trust_domain>/system/<location_path...>/services/<service_label>
 If empty, SPIFFE IDs are not set on health reports or X509 URI SANs.

fields.name: location_path
fields.description:
location_path is this service instance's topology path under /system —
 opaque, tag-delimited, slash-separated segments, arity not fixed
 (e.g. "aws/123456789012/us-east-1a/cluster-7/team-a"). Segments follow the
 SPIFFE segment grammar and must not be reserved tags. Supplied by the
 operator/deployment from runtime config (where the service runs); it is
 not a token claim. May be empty (no topology tiers).

fields.name: disk_persistence
fields.description:
disk_persistence is an init-time/bootstrap setting that enables
 ServiceManager-owned redo-log lifecycle for generated service_store stores.
 When present at ServiceManager creation, the generated ServiceManager opens
 the per-store redo logs, exposes those handles to service code, and owns
 scheduled compaction/roll. It is not hot-reloaded; when absent, typed
 diskstore helpers remain available but no managed roll loop is started.

message.name: DiskPersistenceConfig
message.description:
DiskPersistenceConfig configures the SM-managed persistence component that
 automates the redo-log lifecycle (UC2) for service_store-annotated types.
 It is embedded in the ServiceManager config.

fields.name: roll_interval_seconds
fields.description:
roll_interval_seconds is the compaction/roll period. Also bounds the
 per-node deterministic roll offset (hash(node-id) % roll_interval).

fields.name: archive_count
fields.description: archive_count is how many rolled archive files to retain.

fields.name: dir
fields.description:
dir is the base directory (on the service's own volume) for the
 active / building / temp / archive files.

fields.name: file_permission
fields.description: file_permission is the Unix permission for the data files (e.g. 0600).

message.name: Permission
message.description:
Permission represents Unix-style file permissions (e.g., 755).
 Each field is a 3-bit mask: read (4) + write (2) + execute (1).

fields.name: owner
fields.description: owner permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: group
fields.description: group permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: other
fields.description: other permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: compression
fields.description:
compression for rolled/archived files + snapshots; the live append tail
 stays uncompressed.

fields.name: archive
fields.description:
archive, when set, ships rolled redo segments and daily checkpoints to an
 object store and makes them restorable (Java only; other languages ignore
 it). Unset keeps the local-only behaviour.

message.name: ArchiveConfig
message.description:
ArchiveConfig configures shipping the redo log to an object store. Writes
 are acknowledged locally; shipping is asynchronous and never blocks an
 append. Credentials are the workload's ambient identity (Google Cloud
 Application Default Credentials), never a key in this config.

fields.name: gcs_bucket
fields.description: gcs_bucket is the Google Cloud Storage bucket the archive is written to.

fields.name: prefix
fields.description:
prefix namespaces the archive inside the bucket. Each writer's objects
 live under <prefix>/<member>/<store>/, so several members ship
 independently.

fields.name: checkpoint_interval_seconds
fields.description:
checkpoint_interval_seconds is how often a full checkpoint (the complete
 store state, recording the redo position it covers) is shipped. A restore
 loads the newest checkpoint and replays the segments shipped after it.

fields.name: segment_interval_seconds
fields.description:
segment_interval_seconds is how often the active redo log is rotated and
 shipped as a segment without folding a baseline: the cost is the writes
 since the last rotation, not the store. It is the recovery point after
 losing the volume. 0 (the default) turns rotation off, and the recovery
 point is then one roll_interval_seconds.

fields.name: anonymize_hmac_key
fields.description:
anonymize_hmac_key is the per-deployment data-entitlement ANONYMIZE secret:
 the keyed-HMAC key the generated service wrapper supplies to Sanitize<T> so
 a value pseudonymizes to the same surrogate at any depth, across services
 and restarts. Required only by services whose records carry
 ANONYMIZE-capable (spec.redact) fields — the generated pseudonymize
 primitives fail loud on an empty key.

fields.name: health_probe_port
fields.description:
health_probe_port is the port for a separate PLAINTEXT gRPC listener that
 serves ONLY grpc.health.v1. k8s kubelet probes are plaintext-only and
 cannot speak TLS, so the main TLS port (listen_address) is invisible to
 them. This listener runs on a completely separate grpc.Server / tonic
 Server / NettyServerBuilder with no TLS, no auth interceptors, and no
 business services registered — isolation is the security argument.
 The health status reflects the same StatusSink-driven state as the TLS
 health endpoint: NOT_SERVING until bootstrap completes, then tracks
 handler health (UNHEALTHY → NOT_SERVING, recovery → SERVING).
 Default: 8444. Set to 0 to disable the plaintext health probe listener.

fields.name: config_fetch_timeout_seconds
fields.description:
config_fetch_timeout_seconds bounds the generated state-singleton startup
 fetch. A singleton Get can race the state authority's own convergence and
 return a value that has not been fully seeded yet; the generated fetch()
 retries with the watch-restart backoff for as long as the fetched value
 fails its own generated validate<T>, and fails loudly once this budget is
 spent rather than handing the caller a value it already knows is invalid.
 Must be positive. Default: 30 seconds.

types.description:
ServiceInstanceHealth captures the health, load, and reachability of a
 single running instance of a microservice. The composite key
 "service_id@instance_id" is set by the server from the caller's token claims.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
SPIFFE identity
 spiffe_id is the full SPIFFE URI for this instance, built by the owning
 service manager via the generated sys/spiffe helper (service_spiffe_id) —
 never hand-formatted. It is one of the durable materialization points of
 the computed identity (health identity, X509 URI SAN, workload keys).
 Format: spiffe://<trust_domain>/system/<location...>/services/<service>[/workloads/<child>...]
 Service:  spiffe://example.com/system/aws/us-east-1a/cluster-7/services/identity
 Workload: spiffe://example.com/system/aws/us-east-1a/cluster-7/services/mud-controller/workloads/agent-42
 Consumers needing the location-agnostic service identity parse it with
 service_path_from_spiffe (the bare label, plus any /workloads suffix).

types.name: HttpHeader
types.description: HttpHeader is a single HTTP header name-value pair.

types.name: RawProxyRequest
types.description:
RawProxyRequest forwards an arbitrary HTTP request to a remote REST API.
 Used as the generic fallback RPC for endpoints that do not yet have typed
 RPCs. The service implementation should log when this is used, signaling
 a typed RPC coverage gap.

fields.name: metadata
fields.description:
metadata is an opaque string passed to OPA for policy evaluation.
 OPA resolves the real destination URL; if empty, the service falls back to its DEFAULT_API_ENDPOINT.

fields.name: method
fields.description: method is the HTTP method to use.

fields.name: path
fields.description: path is the API path (e.g. "/repos/owner/repo/issues").

fields.name: query_params
fields.description: query_params are URL query parameters appended to the path.

fields.name: headers
fields.description:
headers are additional HTTP headers to include in the request.
 Authentication headers are injected by the service from config.

message.name: HttpHeader
message.description: HttpHeader is a single HTTP header name-value pair.

fields.name: body
fields.description: body is the request body (typically JSON).

types.name: RawProxyResponse
types.description: RawProxyResponse is the response from a generic proxy request.

fields.name: status_code
fields.description: status_code is the HTTP status code from the upstream API.

fields.name: headers
fields.description: headers are the response headers from the upstream API.

message.name: HttpHeader
message.description: HttpHeader is a single HTTP header name-value pair.

fields.name: body
fields.description: body is the response body (typically JSON).

types.name: HttpClientConfig
types.description:
HttpClientConfig represents configuration for an HTTP client.
 It provides settings for TLS verification, keep-alive behavior, certificates, and timeouts.
 This configuration is typically used to create HTTP clients for making outbound requests
 with specific security and performance requirements.

fields.name: disable_keep_alives
fields.description:
DisableKeepAlives, if true, disables HTTP keep-alives and will close the connection
 after each request. This can reduce server load but increases latency for repeated requests.
 Default is false (keep-alives enabled).

fields.name: root_certs
fields.description:
RootCerts is a list of X.509 certificates to use as root CAs for verifying server certificates.
 If empty, the system's default root CAs will be used.
 Use this to trust custom or internal certificate authorities.

message.name: X509Cert
message.description:
ProtoCert represents an X.509 certificate.
 The certificate is stored as a base64-encoded PEM block.
 Use NewProtoCert() in Go with DER-encoded certificate bytes to create.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is a unique identifier for the certificate

fields.name: base64
fields.description: Base64 contains the base64url-encoded PEM certificate block

fields.name: client_cert
fields.description:
ClientCert is an X.509 certificate chain with private key for client authentication.
 Use this when the server requires mutual TLS (mTLS) authentication.
 chain[0] is the leaf cert, key must be set for mTLS.

message.name: X509CertChain
message.description:
X509CertChain contains a certificate chain and optional private key.
 chain[0] is the leaf (end-entity) cert, followed by intermediates, ordered toward root.
 When key is present, the chain is a full credential suitable for TLS.

fields.name: chain
fields.description: chain[0] is the leaf (end-entity) cert, followed by intermediates, ordered toward root.

fields.name: key
fields.description: optional private key for the leaf cert; present when chain is a full credential.

message.name: Key
message.description: Key represents a private cryptographic key (alias for ProtoKey).

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is a unique identifier for the key (corresponds to kid in JWK)

fields.name: base64
fields.description: Base64 contains the base64url-encoded PEM private key block

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created
 Valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is an optional stable key for chain collections.

fields.name: timeout_seconds
fields.description:
TimeoutSeconds is the maximum time in seconds for the entire HTTP request/response cycle.
 This includes connection time, request writing, server processing, and response reading.
 A value of 0 uses the generated client default of 30 seconds.

fields.name: max_idle_conns
fields.description:
MaxIdleConns controls the maximum number of idle (keep-alive) connections across all hosts.
 A value of 0 means no limit. Default is typically 100 if not specified.

fields.name: max_idle_conns_per_host
fields.description:
MaxIdleConnsPerHost controls the maximum number of idle (keep-alive) connections per host.
 A value of 0 means use the default (typically 2). Increase for high-throughput scenarios.

fields.name: idle_conn_timeout_seconds
fields.description:
IdleConnTimeoutSeconds is the maximum time in seconds an idle connection will remain
 in the connection pool before being closed. A value of 0 means no limit.

fields.name: tls_handshake_timeout_seconds
fields.description:
TlsHandshakeTimeoutSeconds is the maximum time in seconds to wait for a TLS handshake.
 A value of 0 means no timeout. Recommended: 10 seconds.

fields.name: expect_continue_timeout_seconds
fields.description:
ExpectContinueTimeoutSeconds is the maximum time in seconds to wait for a server's
 first response headers after fully writing the request headers if the request has
 "Expect: 100-continue" header. A value of 0 means no timeout.

fields.name: response_header_timeout_seconds
fields.description:
ResponseHeaderTimeoutSeconds is the maximum time in seconds to wait for a server's
 response headers after fully writing the request (including body, if any).
 A value of 0 means no timeout.

fields.name: retry_config
fields.description:
RetryConfig configures retry behavior for HTTP requests.
 If not specified, default retry configuration will be used (3 retries, jittered exponential backoff).

message.name: RetryConfig
message.description:
RetryConfig configures retry behavior for HTTP requests with jittered exponential backoff.
 This configuration controls how failed requests are retried, including which errors
 and status codes trigger retries, and the backoff timing between attempts.

fields.name: max_retries
fields.description:
MaxRetries is the maximum number of retry attempts after the initial request.
 A value of 0 means no retries (only the initial request is made).
 Default: 3

fields.name: initial_backoff_ms
fields.description:
InitialBackoffMs is the initial backoff duration in milliseconds before the first retry.
 This value is multiplied by BackoffMultiplier for each subsequent retry.
 Default: 100ms

fields.name: max_backoff_ms
fields.description:
MaxBackoffMs is the maximum backoff duration in milliseconds.
 The backoff will never exceed this value, even after many retries.
 Default: 5000ms (5 seconds)

fields.name: backoff_multiplier
fields.description:
BackoffMultiplier is the multiplier applied to the backoff duration after each retry.
 For exponential backoff, use values like 2.0 (doubles each time).
 For linear backoff, use 1.0 (stays constant).
 Default: 2.0

fields.name: retryable_status_codes
fields.description:
RetryableStatusCodes are HTTP status codes that should trigger a retry.
 Common retryable codes: 429 (Too Many Requests), 500, 502, 503, 504.
 If empty, defaults to [429, 500, 502, 503, 504].
 Network errors (connection failures, timeouts) are always retried regardless of this setting.

types.name: Jwk
types.description:
Jwk represents a JSON Web Key as defined in RFC 7517.
 It contains the public key parameters for RSA (e, n), EC (crv, x, y), or OKP (crv, x) keys.
 JWK is used for key distribution and verification in JSON-based protocols like JWT.

fields.name: kty
fields.description: Kty is the key type parameter (RSA, EC, or OKP)

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_RSA
enum_values.description: KeyTypeRsa represents an RSA key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_EC
enum_values.description: KeyTypeEc represents an Elliptic Curve key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_OKP
enum_values.description: KeyTypeOkp represents an Octet Key Pair (EdDSA) key type

fields.name: alg
fields.description: Alg is the algorithm intended for use with the key (e.g., "RS384", "ES256", "EdDSA")

fields.name: kid
fields.description: Kid is the key ID used to match keys with signatures

fields.name: use
fields.description: Use indicates the intended use of the key (sig for signatures, enc for encryption)

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_SIG
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeSig indicates the key is used for digital signatures

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_ENC
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeEnc indicates the key is used for encryption

fields.name: e
fields.description: E is the RSA public exponent (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: n
fields.description: N is the RSA modulus (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: crv
fields.description: Crv is the elliptic curve name (e.g., P-256, P-384, P-521, Ed25519)

fields.name: x
fields.description: X is the x coordinate for EC keys or the public key for OKP (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: y
fields.description: Y is the y coordinate for EC keys (base64url encoded without padding, not used for OKP)

fields.name: exp
fields.description:
Exp is the expiration in epoch seconds. This is not part of the JWK spec as the spec does
 not specify how to handle public key expiration.
 When stored in a collection with epoch_expiration, the state store computes TTL = exp - now
 and auto-evicts the entry on expiry.

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created (optional).
 If set, valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

types.name: Jwks
types.description:
Jwks represents a JSON Web Key Set (JWKS) as defined in RFC 7517.
 It contains an array of JWK objects, typically published at a well-known endpoint
 for key distribution and public key verification.

fields.name: keys
fields.description: Keys is the array of JWK objects in this key set

message.name: Jwk
message.description:
Jwk represents a JSON Web Key as defined in RFC 7517.
 It contains the public key parameters for RSA (e, n), EC (crv, x, y), or OKP (crv, x) keys.
 JWK is used for key distribution and verification in JSON-based protocols like JWT.

types.name: OpenIdConfiguration
types.description:
OpenIdConfiguration represents an OpenID Connect Discovery document as defined in OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0.
 It contains the configuration metadata of an OpenID Provider, including endpoint URLs and supported capabilities.
 Typically retrieved from the /.well-known/openid-configuration endpoint.

message.name: Jwk
message.description:
Jwk represents a JSON Web Key as defined in RFC 7517.
 It contains the public key parameters for RSA (e, n), EC (crv, x, y), or OKP (crv, x) keys.
 JWK is used for key distribution and verification in JSON-based protocols like JWT.

fields.name: kty
fields.description: Kty is the key type parameter (RSA, EC, or OKP)

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_RSA
enum_values.description: KeyTypeRsa represents an RSA key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_EC
enum_values.description: KeyTypeEc represents an Elliptic Curve key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_OKP
enum_values.description: KeyTypeOkp represents an Octet Key Pair (EdDSA) key type

fields.name: alg
fields.description: Alg is the algorithm intended for use with the key (e.g., "RS384", "ES256", "EdDSA")

fields.name: kid
fields.description: Kid is the key ID used to match keys with signatures

fields.name: use
fields.description: Use indicates the intended use of the key (sig for signatures, enc for encryption)

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_SIG
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeSig indicates the key is used for digital signatures

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_ENC
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeEnc indicates the key is used for encryption

fields.name: e
fields.description: E is the RSA public exponent (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: n
fields.description: N is the RSA modulus (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: crv
fields.description: Crv is the elliptic curve name (e.g., P-256, P-384, P-521, Ed25519)

fields.name: x
fields.description: X is the x coordinate for EC keys or the public key for OKP (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: y
fields.description: Y is the y coordinate for EC keys (base64url encoded without padding, not used for OKP)

fields.name: exp
fields.description:
Exp is the expiration in epoch seconds. This is not part of the JWK spec as the spec does
 not specify how to handle public key expiration.
 When stored in a collection with epoch_expiration, the state store computes TTL = exp - now
 and auto-evicts the entry on expiry.

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created (optional).
 If set, valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

types.name: LoggerConfig
types.description:
LoggerConfig represents the configuration for a logger instance.
 It controls the output format, verbosity level, and formatting options.

 Example usage:
   - Development mode with console output and pretty printing for local debugging
   - Production mode with JSON output and no pretty printing for log aggregation

fields.name: name
fields.description: Name is the logger name/component identifier

fields.name: format
fields.description:
Format determines the output format for log messages (JSON or console)
 Default: FORMAT_JSON in production, FORMAT_CONSOLE in development

enum_values.name: FORMAT_JSON
enum_values.description: FORMAT_JSON outputs logs as JSON objects, ideal for structured logging and log aggregation systems

enum_values.name: FORMAT_CONSOLE
enum_values.description: FORMAT_CONSOLE outputs logs in a human-readable console format, ideal for development and debugging

fields.name: level
fields.description:
Level sets the minimum severity level for log messages to be output
 Messages below this level will be filtered out
 Default: LEVEL_INFO in production, LEVEL_DEBUG in development

enum_values.name: LEVEL_TRACE
enum_values.description: LEVEL_TRACE is the most verbose log level, used for detailed debugging information

enum_values.name: LEVEL_DEBUG
enum_values.description: LEVEL_DEBUG is used for debugging information, less verbose than trace

enum_values.name: LEVEL_INFO
enum_values.description: LEVEL_INFO is used for informational messages about normal operations

enum_values.name: LEVEL_WARN
enum_values.description: LEVEL_WARN is used for warning messages about potentially problematic situations

enum_values.name: LEVEL_ERROR
enum_values.description: LEVEL_ERROR is used for error messages about failures and problems

fields.name: development
fields.description:
Development enables development mode which:
   - Uses console format by default
   - Enables stack traces for warnings and errors
   - Uses more human-readable timestamps
 Default: false (production mode)

fields.name: pretty_print
fields.description:
PrettyPrint enables pretty-printed output for JSON format
 This makes JSON logs more readable but increases output size
 Should be disabled in production for performance
 Default: false

fields.name: output_paths
fields.description:
OutputPaths is a list of file paths or URLs to write logs to
 Use "stdout" or "stderr" for console output
 Example: ["stdout", "/var/log/app.log"]
constraints: must be a valid file path (type: PATH_ANY)

fields.name: error_output_paths
fields.description:
ErrorOutputPaths is a list of file paths or URLs to write error logs to
 Use "stderr" for console error output
 Example: ["stderr", "/var/log/app-errors.log"]
constraints: must be a valid file path (type: PATH_ANY)

fields.name: disable_caller
fields.description:
DisableCaller disables automatic inclusion of caller information (file:line) in log entries
 Default: false (caller information is included)

fields.name: disable_stacktrace
fields.description:

types.name: McpRequest
types.description: McpRequest carries one JSON-RPC frame from an MCP client to the service.

fields.name: payload
fields.description:
payload is one complete JSON-RPC 2.0 message, serialized.

 Client frames are tool calls and protocol handshakes, both small; the
 bound is a ceiling on a malformed or hostile frame, not a working limit.

types.name: McpResponse
types.description: McpResponse carries one JSON-RPC frame from the service back to the client.

fields.name: payload
fields.description:
payload is one complete JSON-RPC 2.0 message, serialized.

 A tool result holding a page of records is the large case, so this bound
 is well above the 32 KB default for an unannotated string. It sits under
 the 4 MiB gRPC message default so that a frame the service is willing to
 validate is also one an ordinary client will accept; a handler turns an
 over-size result into a JSON-RPC error on that request rather than failing
 the whole stream.

message.name: Jwk
message.description:
Jwk represents a JSON Web Key as defined in RFC 7517.
 It contains the public key parameters for RSA (e, n), EC (crv, x, y), or OKP (crv, x) keys.
 JWK is used for key distribution and verification in JSON-based protocols like JWT.

fields.name: kty
fields.description: Kty is the key type parameter (RSA, EC, or OKP)

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_RSA
enum_values.description: KeyTypeRsa represents an RSA key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_EC
enum_values.description: KeyTypeEc represents an Elliptic Curve key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_OKP
enum_values.description: KeyTypeOkp represents an Octet Key Pair (EdDSA) key type

fields.name: alg
fields.description: Alg is the algorithm intended for use with the key (e.g., "RS384", "ES256", "EdDSA")

fields.name: kid
fields.description: Kid is the key ID used to match keys with signatures

fields.name: use
fields.description: Use indicates the intended use of the key (sig for signatures, enc for encryption)

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_SIG
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeSig indicates the key is used for digital signatures

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_ENC
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeEnc indicates the key is used for encryption

fields.name: e
fields.description: E is the RSA public exponent (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: n
fields.description: N is the RSA modulus (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: crv
fields.description: Crv is the elliptic curve name (e.g., P-256, P-384, P-521, Ed25519)

fields.name: x
fields.description: X is the x coordinate for EC keys or the public key for OKP (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: y
fields.description: Y is the y coordinate for EC keys (base64url encoded without padding, not used for OKP)

fields.name: exp
fields.description:
Exp is the expiration in epoch seconds. This is not part of the JWK spec as the spec does
 not specify how to handle public key expiration.
 When stored in a collection with epoch_expiration, the state store computes TTL = exp - now
 and auto-evicts the entry on expiry.

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created (optional).
 If set, valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

types.name: EventAnnotation
types.description:
EventAnnotation marks a message as an EventBus event: tacplus generates a topic
 and a publish RPC for it. The producer surface is declared (not defaulted):
 set c2s to expose the publish RPC to external clients (via gateway), s2s to
 expose it to internal services. At least one must be present; an internal-only
 event sets only s2s and is never exposed externally. spec.record implies
 spec.event (a record is an event that is also stored + projectable).

fields.name: c2s
fields.description: c2s, when present, exposes the publish RPC to external clients (via gateway).

message.name: MethodC2SAnnotation
message.description:
MethodC2SAnnotation overrides service-level defaults for a single C2S RPC.
 Only valid on methods within a service_c2s service.

fields.name: auth_disabled
fields.description:
auth_disabled: no token required for this RPC.
 Used for public endpoints like OIDC discovery and JWKS.

fields.name: auth_any_user
fields.description:
auth_any_user: any authenticated user can call this RPC
 (no entitlement check). Used for user-facing endpoints where
 any valid token is sufficient (e.g., token exchange, event streams).

fields.name: target_namespace_field
fields.description:
target_namespace_field names the request field whose string value carries

fields.name: routing_only_services
fields.description:
routing_only_services narrows the TYPE a named subscriber's generated
 handler receives. Only meaningful on s2s_subscribe (the consumer half of a
 record/event surface); ignored everywhere else.

 Listing a service here GRANTS it nothing. Authorization stays auth_services'
 job alone; this field only narrows what an already-authorized subscriber's
 generated code is typed to see. auth_services keeps its existing meaning
 unchanged, and a subscriber not listed here keeps receiving the full
 message exactly as before (this is additive).

 For a listed subscriber, tacplus synthesizes

   message <T>RoutingEnvelope {
     string delivery_id = 1;  // <T>'s (spec.record).key field
     string recipient   = 2;  // <T>'s (spec.store_principal) field
     string namespace   = 3;  // <T>'s (spec.store_namespace) field
   }

 and that subscriber's generated Handler takes <T>RoutingEnvelope instead of
 <T>. Generation FAILS for a type flagged here that declares no
 (spec.store_principal) field (and likewise no (spec.record).key or
 (spec.store_namespace) field, or one of the three that is not a string):
 an envelope with an empty recipient is a routing table nobody can route
 with, so it is refused rather than emitted.

 WHAT THIS IS NOT. This is a TYPED boundary, not a memory guarantee. The
 FULL message body still arrives on the wire and is still fully decoded
 inside the subscriber's process; the generated dispatch projects the three
 fields out and drops the decoded message immediately afterwards. The body
 is therefore still reachable from a heap dump, a debugger, or anything that
 logs the decode buffer. What this field delivers is that the subscriber's
 own handler CANNOT be written against the body, because its argument type
 does not have one. Narrowing the wire itself is a separate, broker-side
 change and is not what this field does.

types.name: MethodCollection
types.description:
MethodCollection marks an RPC as a collection-returning read and declares its
 shape. The author declares intent plus a bound; tacplus derives transport,
 tiering, flow control, and lifecycle. See docs/API.md for the full model.

fields.name: mode
fields.description: mode is required: SNAPSHOT (finite) or WATCH (open-ended).

enum_values.name: COLLECTION_MODE_SNAPSHOT
enum_values.description:
SNAPSHOT: a finite point-in-time set that terminates. Requires max_items.
 tacplus derives the delivery tier (inline / accumulated-stream / cursor)
 from max_items and the response's max element size.

enum_values.name: COLLECTION_MODE_WATCH
enum_values.description:
WATCH: an open-ended, change-driven stream (snapshot-then-deltas). Forbids
 max_items; uses a bounded replay ring (replay_depth) for resume.

enum_values.name: COLLECTION_MODE_PAGE
enum_values.description:
PAGE: a client-driven, resumable, windowed GET (unary). The caller pages
 through a finite set with an opaque keyset page_token over order_by; each
 page is bounded by page_size (capped at the trust-tier ceiling). Forbids
 max_items/replay_depth. See the archived RPC_PATTERNS_AND_VERBS_PLAN plan §4.

fields.name: order_by
fields.description:
order_by names the response fields that define a stable total order.
 Required for both modes (pagination cursors and the snapshot/delta boundary
 are only coherent over a stable order). tacplus appends a unique tiebreaker
 if these are not already total.

fields.name: max_items
fields.description:
max_items is the required, positive, finite item cap for SNAPSHOT reads.
 It is the routing key: tacplus computes max_items * max_item_bytes to pick
 the delivery tier. Forbidden on WATCH. Zero/unset on SNAPSHOT is an error.

fields.name: replay_depth
fields.description:
replay_depth is the WATCH replay-ring depth (count of retained changes).
 Optional; defaults to a platform constant. Forbidden on SNAPSHOT.

fields.name: default_page_size
fields.description:
default_page_size is the PAGE per-page window used when the request omits
 page_size. Required positive on PAGE; must be <= the trust-tier ceiling.
 Forbidden on SNAPSHOT/WATCH. PAGE only.

fields.name: revision_field
fields.description:
revision_field names the int64 field on the WATCH delta message that
 carries each change's revision — what the replay ring is keyed by and what
 a caller's from_revision resumes against. Optional; defaults to "revision".
 WATCH only.

 It exists because the delta is not always a purpose-built envelope. Where
 it is (<T>WatchChange { item; revision }) the default is right and nothing
 is declared. Where the delta IS the row — an append-only record has no
 update or delete frame to distinguish, so the change is the new row — the
 row names its own sequence, and that name is the row's to choose:
 scottypersonal.ChatEvent carries `seq`, per-owner monotonic, and is
 already the keyset ListChatEvents pages over. Forcing a second int64
 called `revision` onto such a row would mean two ordering fields that must
 agree forever.

 The named field must exist on the delta message and be a singular int64.
 Generation fails otherwise — including for the default — rather than
 emitting a wrapper that only fails later in cargo/javac/go build.
