types.name: RestBrowser
types.description:
RestBrowser makes an RPC's REST route usable as a browser form target, such
 as the callback an identity provider form-posts to (Sign in with Apple's
 response_mode=form_post). Only on an RPC with a REST route; unary only.

fields.name: form_body
fields.description:
form_body accepts an application/x-www-form-urlencoded request body. Each
 pair is read as a JSON string value keyed by proto field name, so it fills
 the request's string fields. A JSON body is still accepted. A key sent
 twice is refused.

fields.name: redirect_field
fields.description:
redirect_field names a singular string field of the response. The route
 answers 303 See Other with Location set to that field's value and
 Cache-Control: no-store, instead of the JSON response body.

types.name: RestMethods
types.description: RestMethods is a wrapper for repeated RestMethod, used in method options.

types.name: RpcAnnotation

fields.name: principal
fields.description: principal is required; RPC_PRINCIPAL_UNSPECIFIED is not a valid declaration.

enum_values.name: RPC_PRINCIPAL_USER
enum_values.description:
RPC_PRINCIPAL_USER: the caller acts as a user identity. Internally that is
 a client calling as a given user; externally it is the actual user.

enum_values.name: RPC_PRINCIPAL_SERVICE
enum_values.description: RPC_PRINCIPAL_SERVICE: the caller acts as a service identity.

enum_values.name: RPC_PRINCIPAL_MCP
enum_values.description:
RPC_PRINCIPAL_MCP: this RPC is declared as an MCP tool rather than a gRPC
 call. tacplus generates the tool schema and a handler interface method the
 service implements by hand; it maps the tool to no gRPC RPC of its own.
 Being a value of this enum rather than a flag is what keeps a DECLARED tool
 from also being a gRPC call: an rpc block holds one principal.

 It is NOT how most tools come to exist. Every user RPC of a service_c2s
 service — not RPC_PRINCIPAL_SERVICE, minus RPC_FLAG_PUBLIC_NO_AUTH and
 RPC_FLAG_SELF_AUTHENTICATES — is published as a tool automatically, with no
 annotation asking for one and with its gRPC call, REST route and
 entitlement grant intact. Declare this principal only for a tool that has
 no gRPC rpc of its own. Authorization is unchanged either way — flags /
 auth_services / target_namespace_field mean the same thing against whatever
 Caller the MCP session captured at handshake as they do against a gRPC
 caller.

 Streaming is a hard generation failure on this principal: the tool-call wire
 format has no representation for a stream. A handler is free to drive a
 Watch internally and fold it into one response.

fields.name: exposure
fields.description: exposure defaults to RPC_EXPOSURE_INTERNAL.

enum_values.name: RPC_EXPOSURE_INTERNAL
enum_values.description: RPC_EXPOSURE_INTERNAL: reachable only from inside the cluster boundary.

enum_values.name: RPC_EXPOSURE_EXTERNAL
enum_values.description: RPC_EXPOSURE_EXTERNAL: reachable from outside the cluster boundary.

fields.name: flags
fields.description: flags is an unordered set; RPC_FLAG_UNSPECIFIED is not a valid entry.

enum_values.name: RPC_FLAG_PUBLIC_NO_AUTH
enum_values.description:
RPC_FLAG_PUBLIC_NO_AUTH: this RPC is a public endpoint that requires no
 caller token at all (OIDC discovery, JWKS). Nothing authenticates the
 caller, because there is nothing to authenticate.

enum_values.name: RPC_FLAG_AUTH_ANY_USER
enum_values.description:
RPC_FLAG_AUTH_ANY_USER: any authenticated user may call, with no
 entitlement check (e.g. token exchange, event streams).

enum_values.name: RPC_FLAG_AUTH_ENTITLED_USERS
enum_values.description:
RPC_FLAG_AUTH_ENTITLED_USERS: only users holding a matching entitlement
 may call. This is today's default policy for user-facing RPCs.

enum_values.name: RPC_FLAG_SELF_AUTHENTICATES
enum_values.description:
RPC_FLAG_SELF_AUTHENTICATES: this RPC carries no bearer token because it
 authenticates the caller from the request body itself (bootstrap token
 minting, cred-pair JWT). The caller interceptor skips it; the handler does
 the authentication. Distinct from RPC_FLAG_PUBLIC_NO_AUTH: the caller is
 still authenticated, just not by the token path.

enum_values.name: RPC_FLAG_MINTS_CREDENTIAL
enum_values.description:
RPC_FLAG_MINTS_CREDENTIAL: this RPC's response mints or returns a live
 credential — a token, a certificate, a delegate grant — so it is never
 auto-exposed as an MCP tool, whatever its principal. It carries no
 auth/authorizer semantics of its own: a mint RPC's authorization is
 already fully expressed by its principal, its other flags and its
 auth_services. This flag only affects MCP auto-exposure.

fields.name: auth_services
fields.description:
auth_services lists the service identities allowed to call this RPC.
 ["*"] = any authenticated service. Per-RPC: two RPCs of one service may
 legitimately admit different callers.

 On an RPC_PRINCIPAL_USER rpc of a service_c2s service it ADDS the listed
 service identities to the users the rpc already admits: a user token is
 still authorized by its entitlements, a service token by these patterns,
 and a service not listed is refused. This is how one rpc is "c2s for
 users + s2s for these services"; the handler's Caller is whichever
 identity the verified token names.

fields.name: target_namespace_field
fields.description:
target_namespace_field names the request field whose string value carries
 the target namespace path (e.g. "/io/example/tenant"). When set, the
 authorizer enforces the level-or-below rule: the caller's namespace (from
 the bearer token's `namespace` claim) must equal the target namespace or
 be a strict path-segment ancestor of it. The field must exist on this
 RPC's request message and be of type string.

 Use the proto field name (snake_case as declared), e.g. "tenant_namespace".
 Leave unset for RPCs whose target is implicit (e.g. List* methods that
 scope the response to the caller's subtree at the handler). Under
 RPC_FLAG_AUTH_ANY_USER this instead holds an absolute namespace literal.

fields.name: mcp_tool_name
fields.description:
mcp_tool_name overrides the generated MCP tool name for a
 RPC_PRINCIPAL_MCP rpc. Leave it unset: the default is the RPC name in MCP
 naming convention (snake_case), and the tool description is the rpc's own
 leading // doc comment, so neither is a second surface that can drift from
 the real one. Set it only for the rare RPC whose name does not make a good
 tool name. Must be snake_case ([a-z][a-z0-9_]*), and is only meaningful on
 RPC_PRINCIPAL_MCP — declaring it elsewhere fails generation rather than
 being silently ignored.

fields.name: auth_actors
fields.description:
auth_actors lists the delegate identities allowed to call this RPC on
 another principal's behalf. Entries are matched against the token's `act`
 claim — the delegate's service path, the same shape auth_services patterns
 already match — as anchored RE2; ["*"] = any actor.

 The gate runs before the auth_services / entitlement checks, and only when
 the token actually carries `act`: a token with no `act` claim is authorized
 exactly as it is today. A token that DOES carry `act` is rejected unless
 this RPC declares auth_actors and one of its patterns matches, so an RPC
 that says nothing about delegation admits no delegated call at all.

fields.name: requires_device
fields.description:
requires_device declares the DEVICE-ONLY APPROVAL check: this RPC is served
 only when the caller presents a pending approval the person consumed with a
 WebAuthn assertion from a device linked to them. A browser IdP session, a
 delegated agent token and a tenant admin all fail it, however completely
 they are the user.

 The generated server check reads `x-tacplus-approval-id` and
 `x-tacplus-device-assertion-bin` off the call metadata — never request
 fields, so neither is inside the hashed bytes — computes the canonical hash
 of the request, and calls the broker rpc of the (spec.approval_broker)
 service, which must be in the run. Any failure refuses the RPC: the handler
 is never reached. The S2S client for that call is auto-injected into the
 declaring package; the author writes only this boolean.

 The proposing half (creating the pending approval) is the caller's own
 call, not generated. The caller-side generated helper computes the request
 hash with the SAME canonicalization the check uses and attaches the two
 metadata keys.

fields.name: requires_device_when
fields.description:
requires_device_when narrows the same DEVICE-ONLY APPROVAL check above to
 the requests where ONE named request field holds ONE named value. It exists
 for the unified-CRUD shape: an rpc that writes three kinds of row, only one
 of which is a decision about another person, where marking the whole rpc
 would gate the two that are not.

 It is mutually exclusive with requires_device: a conditional gate is a
 narrower requires_device, not an addition to it. Everything else is
 identical — when the condition holds, the SAME check runs over the SAME
 canonical hash of the WHOLE request, so every structural precondition
 (verified caller, plain unary rpc, no map field in the request tree) still
 applies to the whole rpc, unconditionally.

message.name: RequiresDeviceWhen
message.description:
RequiresDeviceWhen is the condition (spec.rpc).requires_device_when gates on.
 Both halves are resolved at generation time against the rpc's request
 descriptor: an unknown field, a field that is not a plain string or enum, or
 an enum value name the enum does not have all fail generation rather than
 becoming a comparison that is silently never true.

fields.name: field
fields.description:
field is a top-level field name on the RPC's request message. It must be a
 plain (non-repeated, non-map, no explicit presence) string or enum field.

fields.name: equals
fields.description:
equals is the value that field must hold for the gate to apply — the enum
 value's short name (e.g. "RULE_EFFECT_DELEGATION") for an enum field, or
 the literal string for a string field.

types.name: ServiceAnnotation
types.description: ServiceAnnotation declares the owning service identity for a proto file.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the canonical service name (e.g. "identity", "gateway").

fields.name: store
fields.description:
store declares this service as a backing store.
 Other services reference it via StateAnnotation.label.

fields.name: config_store
fields.description:
config_store declares this service as THE backing store for auto-injected
 per-service config state (the <Service>ConfigState messages tacplus injects
 from (spec.grpc_config)). At most one service in a proto set may set it.
 Distinct from store: store says "this service can back state", config_store
 says which one config is routed to. Without it, a proto set with more than
 one store has no non-arbitrary answer.

fields.name: gateway
fields.description:
gateway declares this service as a gateway (reverse proxy).
 Changes TLS source to GatewayTlsState (public cert) instead of X509Mint (internal CA).
 The generated run() watches GatewayTlsState for cert hot-reload instead of running
 a TLS renewal loop.

fields.name: rest_dispatch
fields.description:
rest_dispatch generates REST→gRPC dispatch code for all C2S RPCs visible
 to this service. The service acts as a reverse proxy, translating HTTP/JSON
 requests into typed gRPC calls. Used by gateway and the CLI.

fields.name: accepted_audiences
fields.description:
accepted_audiences widens the set of token `aud` values this service's
 generated Authorizer accepts, beyond the two it already derives: its own
 service label, plus every vservice/trait it hosts (AcceptedAudiencesForHost).
 Omitting it — which every service does today — leaves that derived set
 exactly as it is, so this field is backward compatible by construction.

 Declaring an audience here does NOT grant anything. It only stops the
 Authorizer rejecting a token that was correctly minted for that audience;
 the caller must still be entitled to the RPC. Who may add an entry is not a
 runtime question: this is a proto annotation under VCS and code review, the
 same trust boundary as (spec.trait) or an entitlement declaration.

fields.name: tenant_owned
fields.description:
tenant_owned declares this service as a per-tenant instance: the operator
 runs one deployment per tenant, and the service's SPIFFE identity is
 spiffe://<td>/tenants/<tenant>/services/<name> instead of the shared
 /system/services/<name> every other service gets. Tenant identity comes
 ONLY from the caller's token namespace at runtime — this annotation does
 not carry a tenant, it only declares that the service is instantiated
 per-tenant. Read by the operator (per-tenant Deployments), the gateway
 (route by token namespace), and the record-plane store wrapper (tenant
 pin on S2S reads). Default false — every service today is shared.

fields.name: pinned_tenant
fields.description:
pinned_tenant pins a tenant-owned service to exactly one tenant. Meaningful
 ONLY alongside tenant_owned = true: when set, the operator instantiates
 exactly one instance of the service, in that tenant, and does NOT loop over
 the configured tenants. Identity is unchanged — the instance is still
 spiffe://<td>/tenants/<pinned_tenant>/services/<name>; only the cardinality
 changes. This is for a fleet-singleton service that lives in a reserved
 tenant (one row per person, not one row per company), where per-tenant
 replication would split the rows the service exists to hold. The operator
 FAILS reconciliation if the named tenant is not configured: a pin to a
 tenant that does not exist is a config error, not an instance to skip
 silently. Empty — the default, and what every service today carries —
 leaves tenant_owned's per-tenant replication exactly as it is.

types.name: ServiceC2DAnnotation
types.description:
ServiceC2DAnnotation declares a client-to-daemon gRPC service.
 Served over local IPC between CLI processes and a daemon.
 No auth required — filesystem permissions are the security boundary.

fields.name: socket_path
fields.description:
All c2d services are unauthenticated and localhost-only.

 socket_path is the Unix domain socket the daemon binds and clients dial.
 Required — there is no default. A shared default path would collide between
 daemons on the same host, so every c2d service declares its own path.

types.name: ServiceC2SAnnotation
types.description:
ServiceC2SAnnotation declares a client-to-service gRPC service.
 Exposed through the gateway to end users.
 Per-RPC auth lives on spec.rpc: an RPC declares its own policy through
 RPC_FLAG_PUBLIC_NO_AUTH / RPC_FLAG_AUTH_ANY_USER / RPC_FLAG_AUTH_ENTITLED_USERS.
 Default policy: entitled users (gateway enforces entitlements).

fields.name: auth_entitled_users
fields.description:
auth_entitled_users: users with matching entitlements can call.
 This is the default C2S policy; set explicitly when entitlement
 checks are required for all RPCs in this service.

fields.name: label
fields.description:
label is the routing label for the physical service that hosts this C2S
 interface, the twin of (spec.service_s2s).label. A trait declares its
 client-facing surface in its own proto and names the implementor here, so
 the surface is not locked to the implementor's identity.

 The label names the HOST (whom the gateway dials). The AUDIENCE the
 gateway checks the caller's token against is the file's (spec.trait).name,
 not this label: the audience is the contract, so a second implementor of
 the same trait needs no client change. A label no loaded service serves
 fails generation, and so does a label on a file that declares no trait.

types.name: ServiceEventAnnotation
types.description:
ServiceEventAnnotation declares that a state service's topic/queue RPCs
 are accessible to other services (S2S only, like service_state).

fields.name: label
fields.description: label is the routing label for service resolution (e.g. "eventbus").

fields.name: export
fields.description: export makes this event topic available for RO import by other services.

types.name: ServiceHealthAnnotation
types.description:
ServiceHealthAnnotation declares a typed health message for a service.
 The annotated message MUST embed healthreport.ServiceInstanceHealth as field 1
 ("base"). The state store extracts .base for the generic health view and stores the
 full typed message per service (keyed by instance_id).
 Each node reports its own perspective of cluster health — Sentinel monitors
 consistency across perspectives and raises alarms on divergence.

types.name: ServiceS2SAnnotation
types.description:
ServiceS2SAnnotation declares a service-to-service gRPC service.
 Only authenticated service identities can call these RPCs.
 Per-RPC auth lives on spec.rpc: allowed callers (auth_services) and the
 bootstrap corner cases (RPC_FLAG_SELF_AUTHENTICATES) are declared there.

fields.name: auth_services
fields.description:
auth_services: service identities allowed to call (service-level default).
 ["*"] = any service. Named entries restrict to those identities.
 Overridden per-RPC by spec.rpc auth_services; tacplus-generated service
 protos (state, record_map, timeseries, opa_eval) still declare it here.

fields.name: label
fields.description:
label is the routing label for the physical service that hosts this S2S
 interface. Used for vservice routing tables where the interface is defined
 in a vservice proto but hosted by a physical service (e.g. "recordstore").

fields.name: auth_services_from_fleet
fields.description:
auth_services_from_fleet: the caller list is not this proto's to know. The
 fleet build fills auth_services with every service in the fleet that
 declares (spec.grpc_s2s_client) of this service, in the merged tree it
 hands to each service's generation. A standalone build of this proto
 generates with no callers allowed (the authorizers fail closed). Mutually
 exclusive with a literal auth_services.

types.name: ServiceStoreAnnotation
types.description:
ServiceStoreAnnotation marks a message as a durable key-value store.
 Unlike service_state (convergent, fan-out, Watch), service_store is:
   - Write-with-quorum (writes acked only after replication to 2+ nodes)
   - Read-on-demand (no Watch streams, no client-side caching)
   - No boundary decomposition (the message IS the value)
 The store_key field annotation marks which field is the entry key.
 Access is via delegate pattern: services authenticate clients, then
 write through the backing service. External clients never write directly.
types.schema_json:
{
  "name": "ServiceStoreAnnotation",
  "package": "spec",
  "description": "ServiceStoreAnnotation marks a message as a durable key-value store.\n Unlike service_state (convergent, fan-out, Watch), service_store is:\n   - Write-with-quorum (writes acked only after replication to 2+ nodes)\n   - Read-on-demand (no Watch streams, no client-side caching)\n   - No boundary decomposition (the message IS the value)\n The store_key field annotation marks which field is the entry key.\n Access is via delegate pattern: services authenticate clients, then\n write through the backing service. External clients never write directly.",
  "fields": [
    {
      "name": "label",
      "type": "string",
      "description": "label lists the routing labels for the backing stores this store routes to\n (e.g. [\"state-store\"]). Every label must be served by a loaded service; a\n label no service serves fails generation.",
      "repeated": true,
      "constraints": [
        "maximum size: 1024 elements (default)",
        "maximum element size: 32768 bytes (default)"
      ],
      "constraint_infos": [
        {
          "rule": "default_max_size",
          "target": "field",
          "value_kind": "int",
          "int_value": 1024,
          "defaulted": true,
          "unit": "elements",
          "source": "default_bound"
        },
        {
          "rule": "default_max_element_size",
          "target": "element",
          "value_kind": "int",
          "int_value": 32768,
          "defaulted": true,
          "unit": "bytes",
          "source": "default_bound"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

fields.name: label
fields.description:
label lists the routing labels for the backing stores this store routes to
 (e.g. ["state-store"]). Every label must be served by a loaded service; a
 label no service serves fails generation.

types.name: SmbAnnotation
types.description:
SmbAnnotation marks a Service Mesh Blackbox service and selects its trust root.
 The default root is SMB_ROOT_ISOLATED.

enum_values.name: SMB_ROOT_ISOLATED
enum_values.description: SMB_ROOT_ISOLATED uses a self-signed per-SMB CA, scoped only to this SMB.

enum_values.name: SMB_ROOT_CLUSTER
enum_values.description: SMB_ROOT_CLUSTER signs the per-SMB intermediate under the cluster CA.

types.name: SmbAuthorityAnnotation
types.description:
SmbAuthorityAnnotation marks the consumer service that issues per-SMB CAs and
 member certs for spec.smb services (SPIFFE plan D7), declared
 EXPLICITLY rather than inferred. tacplus resolves the fully-qualified
 package.Service carrying this annotation as the SMB cert authority and fails
 generation if any spec.smb service exists with no authority declared. tacplus
 generates the authority contract and the SMB service's client seam; the
 designated consumer service implements the server side (CA keypair custody,
 member-cert signing, rotation). Exactly one authority should be annotated.
types.schema_json:
{
  "name": "SmbAuthorityAnnotation",
  "package": "spec",
  "description": "SmbAuthorityAnnotation marks the consumer service that issues per-SMB CAs and
 member certs for spec.smb services (SPIFFE plan D7), declared
 EXPLICITLY rather than inferred. tacplus resolves the fully-qualified
 package.Service carrying this annotation as the SMB cert authority and fails
 generation if any spec.smb service exists with no authority declared. tacplus
 generates the authority contract and the SMB service's client seam; the
 designated consumer service implements the server side (CA keypair custody,
 member-cert signing, rotation). Exactly one authority should be annotated.",
  "fields": []
}

types.name: StateAnnotation
types.description: StateAnnotation marks a message as a state root and references its backing store.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the state root name (e.g. "ClusterState", "AegisState").

fields.name: label
fields.description:
label lists the routing labels for the backing stores this state root
 routes to (e.g. ["state-store"], ["kernel", "edge"]). Every label must be
 served by a loaded service; a label no service serves fails generation.

fields.name: auto_tls
fields.description:
auto_tls enables automatic TLS certificate lifecycle management.
 When set, tacplus generates a bidi stream subscription to the certificate
 authority service and a new_tls_cert Handler method for cert delivery.
 The service generates keypairs locally; the certificate authority signs and
 delivers certs, triggering renewal at half-life.

enum_values.name: TLS_KEY_TYPE_NONE
enum_values.description: TLS_KEY_TYPE_NONE disables auto-TLS (default).

enum_values.name: TLS_KEY_TYPE_ED25519
enum_values.description: TLS_KEY_TYPE_ED25519 uses Ed25519 (OKP) keys.

enum_values.name: TLS_KEY_TYPE_ECDSA
enum_values.description: TLS_KEY_TYPE_ECDSA uses ECDSA P-256 keys.

fields.name: export
fields.description:
export makes this state root available for RO import by other services.
 Without export, the state is private to the owning service.

fields.name: requires_artifact_on_write
fields.description:
requires_artifact_on_write marks this state root as "the living side" —
 user-owned/user-facing data whose mutation must leave a durable artifact.
 When set, every WRITE-classified RPC (spec.internal/common/verbs registry)
 on a non-synthesized service declared in the same package must be
 accompanied by at least one (spec.record)-annotated message in that
 package; a write RPC with no record in scope fails generation
 (ValidateArtifactOnWrite). Control-plane/config state roots (kernel, opa,
 sentinel, oauth, letsencrypt, operator) must NOT set this — it is only for
 state that represents user-owned knowledge, not service configuration.

fields.name: identity_snapshot
fields.description:
identity_snapshot marks this state root as kernel's OWN identity snapshot
 (decision 2026-09-25: "[Kernel] keeps exactly one durable thing: its OWN
 identity snapshot — signing keys, CAs, tenant tree, grants, links,
 principals") rather than app data parked in a kernel-labelled boundary.
 A field on a state root with this set may carry (spec.persistence) even
 though (spec.service_state).label includes "kernel" — the one exception
 to Rule 3b. Only meaningful on a state root whose label includes
 "kernel"; setting it on any other root does nothing.

types.name: StateImport
types.description:
StateImport is the legacy file-level mirror for field-level state_import
 declarations. The target state must have export=true on its service_state.

fields.name: source
fields.description: source is "package.StateName" (e.g. "identity.Identity", "aegis.AegisState").

types.name: StringConst
types.description:
File-level string constants.
 StringConst defines a named string constant that can be used in file-level options.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Name is the identifier for the constant

fields.name: value
fields.description: Value is the string value of the constant

types.name: SubscriptionAnnotation
types.description:
SubscriptionAnnotation declares that this state service subscribes to
 an event-bus topic from another service's state root.

fields.name: source
fields.description:
source is the fully-qualified topic reference: "package.StateRoot.field_name"
 e.g., "telemetry.AgenticCodeEventBus.event_stream"

types.name: TimeseriesFieldOption

fields.name: order_key
fields.description: Position in the store-neutral sort-key role (1-indexed). 0 = not a sort key.

fields.name: partition_key
fields.description: Part of the store-neutral partition role.

fields.name: cardinality_hint
fields.description: Store-neutral hint about the column's distinct-value count.

types.name: TimeseriesStoreAnnotation
types.description:
TimeseriesStoreAnnotation marks a service proto as a timeseries data store.
 The store receives its projection data by auto-subscribing to the EventBus
 topics that carry its projection sources; no mutation service is generated.

types.name: TimeseriesTypeAnnotation

fields.name: name
fields.description: Table name. Default: snake_case of message name.

fields.name: source
fields.description:
Source event FQN for field extraction.
 When set, every field in this message must have (spec.projection_source) to map
 from the source event to this projection.
 Example: "sensor.SensorEvent"

fields.name: dedup
fields.description: dedup is the store-neutral duplicate-resolution policy.

message.name: DedupPolicy
message.description:
DedupPolicy is a store-neutral statement of row identity and duplicate
 resolution. A downstream materializer maps this onto an engine's merge/dedup
 mechanism; tacplus carries only the semantic intent.

types.name: TokenMinterAnnotation
types.description:
TokenMinterAnnotation marks a service as the cluster's token minter, declared
 EXPLICITLY rather than inferred from RPC signatures. The bootstrap token
 exchanger (service_im / client_im codegen) targets the service carrying this
 annotation, resolving its fully-qualified package.Service. Exactly one
 authoritative minter should be annotated.

fields.name: proxy
fields.description:
proxy marks the client-reachable C2S front (e.g. gateway.Mint) that proxies
 to the authoritative S2S minter. Clients with no S2S identity mint through
 this proxy; services with an S2S identity call the authoritative minter
 (proxy = false) directly.

types.name: TraitAnnotation
types.description:
TraitAnnotation declares a trait identity for a proto file.
 Traits carry the same identity shape as a vservice — a canonical name used as
 the entitlement key plus a stable TokenEntitlements field id — and are parsed
 into the same descriptor fields.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the canonical trait name used as the entitlement key (e.g., "query").

fields.name: id
fields.description: id is the stable field number in TokenEntitlements for this trait.

fields.name: host
fields.description:
host is the routing label of the physical service that implements this
 trait's RPCs. It becomes the (spec.service_s2s)/(spec.service_c2s) label on
 the emitted sibling services, so the gateway dials the host while callers
 are still entitled against `name` — the audience is the contract, not the
 implementor.

fields.name: s2s_service
fields.description:
s2s_service and c2s_service name the sibling services the trait's plane is
 emitted as. A service may declare only one caller surface
 (ValidateServiceSurfaces), so one plane serving both peers and users is two
 services. They are declared rather than derived from `name` so the emitted
 identities are readable in the declaration instead of in generator source.

 s2s_service is required. c2s_service is OPTIONAL: leave it empty and the
 trait hosts the peer half only — no client-facing sibling is emitted and the
 plane contributes no grants to the c2s catalog. A service that wants its own
 records readable by users declares (spec.record_read).c2s, which gives it a
 scoped <Svc>Records plane instead of a share in this fleet-wide one.

fields.name: auth_services
fields.description:
auth_services lists the peer identities allowed to call the S2S half, the
 per-RPC (spec.rpc).auth_services the emitted service carries. Declared here
 rather than hardcoded in the generator: the platform generator must not
 name an application service.

types.name: Transformation
types.description:
Transformation declares a pure typed conversion of this message into a
 derived row type: source message A -> derived type B. tacplus generates the
 derived message with its column annotations and projection_source mappings.

 A transformation says NOTHING about delivery. It does not require the source
 to be a (spec.record), it does not create or subscribe to an EventBus topic,
 and it carries no retention window — retention is delivery-side state and
 lives on (spec.record).retention. Declaring a transformation and declaring
 delivery are independent: either generates without the other.

 The shape is store-neutral: dedup and cardinality_hint are declared as
 semantic intent, and a downstream materializer renders the concrete
 engine/merge behavior.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the derived row type name (e.g. "SessionRecord").

fields.name: when
fields.description:
when is the oneof variant name that triggers this row (e.g. "session").
 Only source messages carrying this payload variant produce a row.

fields.name: field
fields.description: field lists the source fields projected into the derived type.

message.name: TransformationField
message.description: TransformationField maps a source message field to a derived-type column.

fields.name: source
fields.description: source is the field path on the source message (e.g. "session.model").

fields.name: as
fields.description: as renames the column in the derived type (defaults to last segment of source).

fields.name: order_key
fields.description:
order_key is the column's position in the store-neutral sort-key role
 (0 = not a sort key). A materializer maps this to the engine's sort order.

fields.name: partition_key
fields.description: partition_key marks this column as part of the store-neutral partition role.

fields.name: cardinality_hint
fields.description: cardinality_hint is a store-neutral hint about the column's distinct-value count.

fields.name: dedup
fields.description: dedup is the store-neutral duplicate-resolution policy for the derived rows.

message.name: DedupPolicy
message.description:
DedupPolicy is a store-neutral statement of row identity and duplicate
 resolution. A downstream materializer maps this onto an engine's merge/dedup
 mechanism; tacplus carries only the semantic intent.

types.name: TransformationField
types.description: TransformationField maps a source message field to a derived-type column.

fields.name: source
fields.description: source is the field path on the source message (e.g. "session.model").

fields.name: as
fields.description: as renames the column in the derived type (defaults to last segment of source).

fields.name: order_key
fields.description:
order_key is the column's position in the store-neutral sort-key role
 (0 = not a sort key). A materializer maps this to the engine's sort order.

fields.name: partition_key
fields.description: partition_key marks this column as part of the store-neutral partition role.

fields.name: cardinality_hint
fields.description: cardinality_hint is a store-neutral hint about the column's distinct-value count.

types.name: VServiceAnnotation
types.description:
VServiceAnnotation declares a virtual service identity for a proto file.
 Virtual services have their RPCs hosted by a physical service (e.g., eventbus)
 but are authorized separately. The id is a stable field number for TokenEntitlements
 (use range 30+ to avoid collision with physical service IDs).

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the canonical vservice name used as the entitlement key (e.g., "telemetry").

fields.name: id
fields.description: id is the stable field number in TokenEntitlements for this vservice.

types.name: VolumeGroupAnnotation
types.description:
VolumeGroupAnnotation declares one named volume group in the platform blob
 store, owned by the service carrying the annotation. A volume group is a set
 of build-time rules (accepted content types, per-blob size ceiling, per-tenant
 quota) that the blob store enforces at upload; groups are never created at
 runtime, so a service that stores blobs MUST declare its group here. The
 annotation is repeatable: one service may declare several groups. tacplus
 refuses duplicate group names across the whole fleet and surfaces every
 declared group in registry.json so the operator can render the blob store's
 config; tacplus does not implement the blob store.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the volume group's identifier. Must be unique across the whole fleet.

fields.name: max_blob_bytes
fields.description: max_blob_bytes is the largest single blob this group accepts.

fields.name: content_types
fields.description:
content_types is the allow-list of MIME types this group accepts, e.g.
 "application/pdf". Each entry must be a well-formed media type (validated at
 build time; the runtime service still checks magic bytes per-upload).

fields.name: tenant_quota_bytes
fields.description: tenant_quota_bytes is the per-tenant storage quota within this group.

enums.name: IpAddrTypes
enums.description:
IpAddrTypes defines validation types for IP addresses, masks, and networks.
 Used in field options to enforce IP address format validation.

values.name: IP_ADDR_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED
values.description: IP_ADDR_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED represents an unspecified IP address type

values.name: IP_ADDR_TYPE_IP_V4
values.description: IP_ADDR_TYPE_IP_V4 validates IPv4 addresses (e.g., 1.1.1.1)

values.name: IP_ADDR_TYPE_IP_V6
values.description: IP_ADDR_TYPE_IP_V6 validates IPv6 addresses (e.g., 2001:0db8:85a3:0000:0000:8a2e:0370:7334)

values.name: IP_ADDR_TYPE_IP_ANY
values.description: IP_ADDR_TYPE_IP_ANY validates either IPv4 or IPv6 addresses

values.name: IP_ADDR_TYPE_MASK_V4
values.description: IP_ADDR_TYPE_MASK_V4 validates IPv4 subnet masks (e.g., 0-32)

values.name: IP_ADDR_TYPE_MASK_V6
values.description: IP_ADDR_TYPE_MASK_V6 validates IPv6 subnet masks (e.g., 0-128)

values.name: IP_ADDR_TYPE_MASK_ANY
values.description: IP_ADDR_TYPE_MASK_ANY validates either IPv4 or IPv6 subnet masks

values.name: IP_ADDR_TYPE_NET_V4
values.description: IP_ADDR_TYPE_NET_V4 validates IPv4 CIDR networks (e.g., 1.1.1.1/32)

values.name: IP_ADDR_TYPE_NET_V6
values.description: IP_ADDR_TYPE_NET_V6 validates IPv6 CIDR networks (e.g., 2001:0db8:85a3::8a2e:0370:7334/128)

values.name: IP_ADDR_TYPE_NET_ANY
values.description: IP_ADDR_TYPE_NET_ANY validates either IPv4 or IPv6 CIDR networks

enums.name: EncType
enums.description:
EncType defines validation types for cryptographic keys and certificates.
 Used in field options to enforce key format and algorithm validation.

values.name: ENC_TYPE_KEY_UNDEFINED
values.description: ENC_TYPE_KEY_UNDEFINED represents an unspecified encryption key type

values.name: ENC_TYPE_KEY_PRIVATE_RSA
values.description: ENC_TYPE_KEY_PRIVATE_RSA validates private RSA keys in PEM format

values.name: ENC_TYPE_KEY_PUBLIC_RSA
values.description: ENC_TYPE_KEY_PUBLIC_RSA validates public RSA keys in PEM format

values.name: ENC_TYPE_KEY_ANY_RSA
values.description: ENC_TYPE_KEY_ANY_RSA validates either private or public RSA keys

values.name: ENC_TYPE_KEY_PRIVATE_EC
values.description: ENC_TYPE_KEY_PRIVATE_EC validates private Elliptic Curve keys in PEM format

values.name: ENC_TYPE_KEY_PUBLIC_EC
values.description: ENC_TYPE_KEY_PUBLIC_EC validates public Elliptic Curve keys in PEM format

values.name: ENC_TYPE_KEY_ANY_EC
values.description: ENC_TYPE_KEY_ANY_EC validates either private or public EC keys

values.name: ENC_TYPE_KEY_PRIVATE_ED25519
values.description: ENC_TYPE_KEY_PRIVATE_ED25519 validates private Ed25519 keys in PEM format

values.name: ENC_TYPE_KEY_PUBLIC_ED25519
values.description: ENC_TYPE_KEY_PUBLIC_ED25519 validates public Ed25519 keys in PEM format

values.name: ENC_TYPE_KEY_ANY_ED25519
values.description: ENC_TYPE_KEY_ANY_ED25519 validates either private or public Ed25519 keys

values.name: ENC_TYPE_KEY_PRIVATE_ANY
values.description: ENC_TYPE_KEY_PRIVATE_ANY validates private keys of any algorithm (RSA, EC, Ed25519)

values.name: ENC_TYPE_KEY_PUBLIC_ANY
values.description: ENC_TYPE_KEY_PUBLIC_ANY validates public keys of any algorithm

values.name: ENC_TYPE_KEY_ANY
values.description: ENC_TYPE_KEY_ANY validates any key (private or public) of any algorithm

values.name: ENC_TYPE_X509_CERT_RSA
values.description: ENC_TYPE_X509_CERT_RSA validates X.509 certificates with RSA public keys

values.name: ENC_TYPE_X509_CERT_EC
values.description: ENC_TYPE_X509_CERT_EC validates X.509 certificates with EC public keys

values.name: ENC_TYPE_X509_CERT_ED25519
values.description: ENC_TYPE_X509_CERT_ED25519 validates X.509 certificates with Ed25519 public keys

values.name: ENC_TYPE_X509_CERT_ANY
values.description: ENC_TYPE_X509_CERT_ANY validates X.509 certificates with any key algorithm

enums.name: SqlPermit
enums.description:
SqlPermit defines validation types for SQL statement fields.
 Used in field options to enforce a syntactic sanity check plus a statement-type restriction.
 This is NOT an injection defense: the validator only rejects a handful of obvious tokens
 (semicolons, -- and /* comments, backslash escapes) and checks the leading keyword. A
 syntactically valid statement can still carry an injection payload (e.g. a UNION or a
 subquery in a permitted SELECT), and the check does not cover all comment syntaxes (e.g.
 '#' line comments). Callers MUST use parameterized queries and MUST NOT interpolate a validated
 string into a query as though it were safe.

values.name: SQL_PERMIT_UNSPECIFIED
values.description: SQL_PERMIT_UNSPECIFIED represents an unspecified SQL permit type

values.name: SQL_PERMIT_SELECT
values.description: SQL_PERMIT_SELECT allows only SELECT statements (including WITH ... SELECT CTEs)

values.name: SQL_PERMIT_DML
values.description: SQL_PERMIT_DML allows SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE statements

values.name: SQL_PERMIT_DDL
values.description: SQL_PERMIT_DDL allows CREATE, ALTER, DROP, TRUNCATE statements

values.name: SQL_PERMIT_ANY
values.description: SQL_PERMIT_ANY applies only the syntactic sanity check, with no statement-type restriction

enums.name: Azp
enums.description:
Azp enumerates the authorized-party / attestation contexts a kernel-minted
 token may record (SPIFFE plan D4). It is the proto-defined source of truth for
 the `azp` claim — generated code carries no hardcoded azp list. `azp` is the
 attestation path, NOT part of the subject identity, and kernel sets it from
 trusted context (never copied from untrusted request claims).

values.name: AZP_KERNEL
values.description:
kernel: minted by kernel from trusted internal context (service/bootstrap).
 The name is a well-known convention from the first platform, not a
 dependency on a service called kernel: see docs/USER.md "Well-Known
 Names" and https://github.com/tacplus-dev/tacplus/issues/1.

values.name: AZP_OAUTH
values.description:
oauth: user attested via an OAuth broker; kernel maps the broker's
 authenticated S2S identity to this value at MintUserToken.

values.name: AZP_CLOUD_AUTH
values.description:
cloud-auth: reserved for the future cloud-auth attestation broker. No
 runtime mints this except tests until that broker exists (D4).

enums.name: TypeKind
enums.description: TypeKind classifies protobuf field kinds for generated registry metadata.

enums.name: PrincipalScope
enums.description:
PrincipalScope is how wide a caller's authority over PRINCIPALS is. It rides
 the caller's grant as the "principal_scope" key of the OPA-stamped
 service_entitlements claim bag — the same bag the egress "data_grants" ride —
 so it is one more claim on an existing seam, not a second auth path.

 The generated service wrapper reads it by name and compares it to the row's
 principal. SELF_ONLY (and absent/unspecified, which fail closed to it) means
 the caller may act only as its own principal, which is what scopes a
 (spec.owner_default) refusal to the row's owner instead of to every caller.
 Anything wider means the caller is not the owner acting on itself.

 SELF_ONLY, not SELF: the Rust variant is the value name with the enum prefix
 stripped, and `Self` is a Rust keyword that protoc-gen-prost-serde does not
 escape (prost renders `Self_`, the serde companion renders `Self`, and the
 crate does not compile). See PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_QUESTIONS.md.

values.name: PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_UNSPECIFIED
values.description:
Unspecified is the proto3 zero value and is treated as SELF_ONLY: a token
 that says nothing about principal scope has not been widened.

values.name: PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_SELF_ONLY
values.description: Self only: the caller may act only on rows whose principal is the caller.

values.name: PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_SUBTREE
values.description:
Subtree: the caller may act on rows whose principal is at or below the
 caller's own namespace.

values.name: PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_ANY
values.description: Any: the caller may act on any principal's rows.

enums.name: Mutability
enums.description: Mutability is whether a stored record type's rows may change after write.

values.name: MUTABILITY_UNSPECIFIED
values.description: Unspecified = MUTABILITY_CRUD (today's behaviour).

values.name: MUTABILITY_CRUD
values.description: CRUD: rows may be updated and deleted by key.

values.name: MUTABILITY_APPEND_ONLY
values.description:
APPEND_ONLY: rows are written once. No row-mutating RPC is generated for
 the type and the generated wrapper refuses to host one. Its disk slices are
 pure appends — sealed, checksummable units.

enums.name: CardinalityHint
enums.description:
CardinalityHint is a store-neutral hint about how many distinct values a
 column holds. A downstream materializer may use it to pick an encoding, but
 tacplus emits no concrete codec — the hint is pure semantic intent.

enums.name: DedupStrategy
enums.description: DedupStrategy is a store-neutral statement of how duplicate rows are resolved.

enums.name: SmbRoot
enums.description: SmbRoot selects which trust root backs an SMB service's member certificates.

values.name: SMB_ROOT_ISOLATED
values.description: SMB_ROOT_ISOLATED uses a self-signed per-SMB CA, scoped only to this SMB.

values.name: SMB_ROOT_CLUSTER
values.description: SMB_ROOT_CLUSTER signs the per-SMB intermediate under the cluster CA.

enums.name: RpcPrincipal
enums.description:
RpcPrincipal declares WHO calls an RPC: a user identity, a service identity,
 or a model acting through a generated MCP tool surface. They are mutually
 exclusive, so this is an enum rather than a flag. Every spec.rpc must set it —
 there is no safe default, because either wrong answer is a silent
 authorization bug rather than a loud failure.

values.name: RPC_PRINCIPAL_USER
values.description:
RPC_PRINCIPAL_USER: the caller acts as a user identity. Internally that is
 a client calling as a given user; externally it is the actual user.

values.name: RPC_PRINCIPAL_SERVICE
values.description: RPC_PRINCIPAL_SERVICE: the caller acts as a service identity.

values.name: RPC_PRINCIPAL_MCP
values.description:
RPC_PRINCIPAL_MCP: this RPC is declared as an MCP tool rather than a gRPC
 call. tacplus generates the tool schema and a handler interface method the
 service implements by hand; it maps the tool to no gRPC RPC of its own.
 Being a value of this enum rather than a flag is what keeps a DECLARED tool
 from also being a gRPC call: an rpc block holds one principal.

 It is NOT how most tools come to exist. Every user RPC of a service_c2s
 service — not RPC_PRINCIPAL_SERVICE, minus RPC_FLAG_PUBLIC_NO_AUTH and
 RPC_FLAG_SELF_AUTHENTICATES — is published as a tool automatically, with no
 annotation asking for one and with its gRPC call, REST route and
 entitlement grant intact. Declare this principal only for a tool that has
 no gRPC rpc of its own. Authorization is unchanged either way — flags /
 auth_services / target_namespace_field mean the same thing against whatever
 Caller the MCP session captured at handshake as they do against a gRPC
 caller.

 Streaming is a hard generation failure on this principal: the tool-call wire
 format has no representation for a stream. A handler is free to drive a
 Watch internally and fold it into one response.

enums.name: RpcExposure
enums.description:
RpcExposure declares WHERE an RPC is reachable from. Also mutually
 exclusive, so also an enum. Unlike principal it has a safe default:
 forgetting it under-exposes the RPC, which fails loudly at call time rather
 than silently widening the surface.

values.name: RPC_EXPOSURE_INTERNAL
values.description: RPC_EXPOSURE_INTERNAL: reachable only from inside the cluster boundary.

values.name: RPC_EXPOSURE_EXTERNAL
values.description: RPC_EXPOSURE_EXTERNAL: reachable from outside the cluster boundary.

enums.name: RpcFlag
enums.description:
RpcFlag carries the non-exclusive protocol properties of an RPC — the
 things that are independent of principal and exposure and of each other, so
 an RPC may carry any combination of them (including none).

values.name: RPC_FLAG_PUBLIC_NO_AUTH
values.description:
RPC_FLAG_PUBLIC_NO_AUTH: this RPC is a public endpoint that requires no
 caller token at all (OIDC discovery, JWKS). Nothing authenticates the
 caller, because there is nothing to authenticate.

values.name: RPC_FLAG_AUTH_ANY_USER
values.description:
RPC_FLAG_AUTH_ANY_USER: any authenticated user may call, with no
 entitlement check (e.g. token exchange, event streams).

values.name: RPC_FLAG_AUTH_ENTITLED_USERS
values.description:
RPC_FLAG_AUTH_ENTITLED_USERS: only users holding a matching entitlement
 may call. This is today's default policy for user-facing RPCs.

values.name: RPC_FLAG_SELF_AUTHENTICATES
values.description:
RPC_FLAG_SELF_AUTHENTICATES: this RPC carries no bearer token because it
 authenticates the caller from the request body itself (bootstrap token
 minting, cred-pair JWT). The caller interceptor skips it; the handler does
 the authentication. Distinct from RPC_FLAG_PUBLIC_NO_AUTH: the caller is
 still authenticated, just not by the token path.

values.name: RPC_FLAG_MINTS_CREDENTIAL
values.description:
RPC_FLAG_MINTS_CREDENTIAL: this RPC's response mints or returns a live
 credential — a token, a certificate, a delegate grant — so it is never
 auto-exposed as an MCP tool, whatever its principal. It carries no
 auth/authorizer semantics of its own: a mint RPC's authorization is
 already fully expressed by its principal, its other flags and its
 auth_services. This flag only affects MCP auto-exposure.

enums.name: CollectionMode
enums.description:
CollectionMode declares how a multi-result read behaves. See docs/API.md.
 A read returning more than one result must declare exactly one mode; an
 unbounded SNAPSHOT is a contradiction (if it is unbounded, it is a WATCH).

values.name: COLLECTION_MODE_SNAPSHOT
values.description:
SNAPSHOT: a finite point-in-time set that terminates. Requires max_items.
 tacplus derives the delivery tier (inline / accumulated-stream / cursor)
 from max_items and the response's max element size.

values.name: COLLECTION_MODE_WATCH
values.description:
WATCH: an open-ended, change-driven stream (snapshot-then-deltas). Forbids
 max_items; uses a bounded replay ring (replay_depth) for resume.

values.name: COLLECTION_MODE_PAGE
values.description:
PAGE: a client-driven, resumable, windowed GET (unary). The caller pages
 through a finite set with an opaque keyset page_token over order_by; each
 page is bounded by page_size (capped at the trust-tier ceiling). Forbids
 max_items/replay_depth. See the archived RPC_PATTERNS_AND_VERBS_PLAN plan §4.

enums.name: Visibility
enums.description: Visibility is the (spec.visibility) value of a public_view message's field.

enums.name: QueryOp
enums.description: QueryOp is the match kind for a (spec.query_field) record filter criterion.

enums.name: RedactMode
enums.description:
RedactMode selects the data-entitlement transform for a field on its way out
 of a service (egress-only, e.g. Sample/Pull). It expresses the four states of
 the data-entitlement lattice across two transform kinds (redact, anonymize)
 and two floors (hard "is-*", eligible "may-*"). Effective level per field is
 max(annotation floor, runtime entitlement) under pass-through < anonymize <
 redact — the runtime entitlement can only ratchet tighter, never loosen below
 the floor. The two "is-*" modes are the original unconditional behavior.

enums.name: EvictionPolicy
enums.description:
EvictionPolicy determines which entries to evict when max_size is reached.
 Used as a field-level annotation on boundary fields and as a message-level
 default on state root messages.

values.name: EVICTION_POLICY_NONE
values.description: EVICTION_POLICY_NONE disables eviction (default). Entries are never evicted by policy.

values.name: EVICTION_POLICY_LRU
values.description: EVICTION_POLICY_LRU evicts least recently used entries.

values.name: EVICTION_POLICY_LFU
values.description: EVICTION_POLICY_LFU evicts least frequently used entries.

values.name: EVICTION_POLICY_RANDOM
values.description: EVICTION_POLICY_RANDOM evicts entries randomly.

enums.name: MaxSizePolicy
enums.description: MaxSizePolicy determines what the eviction_max_size limit refers to.

values.name: MAX_SIZE_POLICY_ENTRY_COUNT
values.description: MAX_SIZE_POLICY_ENTRY_COUNT limits by total number of entries (default).

values.name: MAX_SIZE_POLICY_USED_HEAP_SIZE
values.description: MAX_SIZE_POLICY_USED_HEAP_SIZE limits by heap memory used in bytes.

values.name: MAX_SIZE_POLICY_USED_HEAP_PERCENTAGE
values.description: MAX_SIZE_POLICY_USED_HEAP_PERCENTAGE limits by percentage of heap memory used.

values.name: MAX_SIZE_POLICY_FREE_HEAP_PERCENTAGE
values.description: MAX_SIZE_POLICY_FREE_HEAP_PERCENTAGE evicts when free heap drops below percentage.

enums.name: TlsKeyType
enums.description: TlsKeyType specifies the key algorithm for auto-TLS certificate management.

values.name: TLS_KEY_TYPE_NONE
values.description: TLS_KEY_TYPE_NONE disables auto-TLS (default).

values.name: TLS_KEY_TYPE_ED25519
values.description: TLS_KEY_TYPE_ED25519 uses Ed25519 (OKP) keys.

values.name: TLS_KEY_TYPE_ECDSA
values.description: TLS_KEY_TYPE_ECDSA uses ECDSA P-256 keys.

enums.name: ConfigSliceScope
enums.description:
ConfigSliceScope identifies the aggregate config message that receives a
 per-service config slice.

enums.name: C2SScope
enums.description:
C2SScope names WHICH ROWS a client-facing record read may return, out of a
 closed set. It is not a predicate language and must never become one.

 Every value here is derivable from VERIFIED TOKEN CLAIMS alone. The moment a
 scope would need something else — "the decider this ticket is routed to", a
 reach down an org hierarchy — it has stopped being a generated backstop and
 become business logic, and such a read belongs in a HAND-WRITTEN RPC whose
 body calls the generated s2s reader. That boundary is the design, not a gap
 in it.

 Declared top-level rather than nested inside RecordReadC2S: a nested enum
 generates but does not compile in the Rust model crate.

values.name: C2S_SCOPE_UNSPECIFIED
values.description:
Unspecified = C2S_SCOPE_PRINCIPAL. The narrowest value is the default, so a
 reader that declares the block and forgets the scope discloses the least,
 not the most.

values.name: C2S_SCOPE_PRINCIPAL
values.description:
PRINCIPAL: rows whose owning-principal field equals the caller's subject,
 AND whose namespace equals the caller's tenant. "My own rows."

 The principal field is resolved exactly as the egress row filter resolves
 it — (spec.store_principal) on a record field, else (spec.record).owner —
 and ONLY when that field is also an EQ criterion on the generated <T>Filter.
 When it resolves to nothing, generation FAILS rather than degrading to a
 tenant-wide read: on ScottyActivity and AccountingRecord the declared
 `owner` is the PUBLISHING SERVICE, so a filter on it would show a human
 every row in its tenant while looking like it showed them their own.

values.name: C2S_SCOPE_NAMESPACE
values.description:
NAMESPACE: every row in the caller's tenant, with no principal narrowing.
 A legitimate shape — an org-wide audit feed — but a disclosure decision, so
 it must be written down and can never be what absence means.

 DECLARED BUT NOT IMPLEMENTED in v1: generation fails with an explicit
 "declared but not implemented" error. The value exists so it cannot be
 invented twice with two meanings.

enums.name: RestMethod
enums.description:
RestMethod enumerates additional HTTP methods for REST exposure.
 POST is always implicit on every convention REST route and does not
 appear in this enum. These values are used with spec.rest_method to
 declare additional HTTP methods for an RPC.

types.name: BoundaryInfo
types.description:
BoundaryInfo describes a state boundary in a tacplus build.
 This is language-neutral metadata exposed by generated registry code.

fields.name: service
fields.description:
Owning service, as the project-specific ServiceName enum. Like
 RpcInfo.service, this is a placeholder POPULATED DOWNSTREAM once the full
 ServiceName enum is generated into generated/services.proto — it is
 SERVICE_NAME_UNSPECIFIED in the base registry tacplus emits (the base enum has
 only UNSPECIFIED/ANY). For the owning-service identifier tacplus actually
 emits, use `label` (field 15), the service_state routing labels.

fields.name: state_root
fields.description: State root message name, e.g. "ClusterState".

fields.name: boundary
fields.description: Boundary field name, e.g. "ClusterInfo".

fields.name: persistence
fields.description:
True when the boundary carries (spec.persistence). No state store implements
 that flag today — kernel is in-memory coordination and holds no durable user
 data; durable data belongs in stored records. Descriptive IR only: tacplus
 carries the flag here for a future store that does implement it, and
 implements nothing itself. Refused outright on a kernel-labelled state root.

fields.name: collection
fields.description: True when the boundary is a collection (repeated field).

fields.name: type_fqn
fields.description: Fully qualified type name of the boundary message.

fields.name: boundary_callers
fields.description: Cross-namespace callers allowed on this boundary field.

fields.name: rpcs
fields.description: RPCs that operate on this boundary (derived from naming convention).

fields.name: is_config
fields.description: True when this boundary is a configuration boundary (ConfigState pattern).

fields.name: label
fields.description:
Routing labels from the service_state annotation (e.g., ["state-store"],
 ["kernel", "edge"]).

fields.name: graph_type
fields.description:
Graph type of this boundary: "singleton", "collection", "topic",
 "queue", "priority_queue", "command", "view", "state_import", "private".

fields.name: auto_tls_key_type
fields.description:
auto_tls_key_type is the key algorithm when auto_tls is enabled ("ed25519" or "ecdsa").
 Empty means auto_tls is disabled.

fields.name: collected_health
fields.description: True when this boundary is marked for Sentinel health collection.

types.name: BuildInfo
types.description: BuildInfo contains version and build metadata for the registry.

fields.name: tacplus_version
fields.description: tacplus version that generated this registry.

fields.name: build_timestamp
fields.description: Timestamp when the registry was generated (RFC 3339).

fields.name: source_git_sha
fields.description: Git SHA of the source proto directory, if available.

types.name: ClientDependencyInfo
types.description: ClientDependencyInfo describes a file-level declared gRPC client dependency.

fields.name: source_package
fields.description: source_package is the proto package that declares the dependency.

fields.name: surface_kind
fields.description: surface_kind is "s2s", "c2s", or "w2s".

fields.name: service
fields.description: service is the declared target service ref, usually "package.ServiceName".

fields.name: target_package
fields.description: target_package is parsed from service when service is package-qualified.

fields.name: target_service
fields.description: target_service is parsed from service when service is package-qualified.

fields.name: wildcard
fields.description: wildcard is true for spec.all_grpc_s2s_clients.

types.name: DedupPolicyInfo
types.description:
DedupPolicyInfo is the registry mirror of spec.DedupPolicy — the store-neutral
 row identity + duplicate-resolution policy. A downstream materializer maps this
 onto an engine's merge/dedup mechanism.

types.name: DependenciesConfig
types.description: DependenciesConfig is the top-level schema for dependencies.yaml.
types.schema_json:
{
  "name": "DependenciesConfig",
  "package": "tacplus",
  "description": "DependenciesConfig is the top-level schema for dependencies.yaml.",
  "fields": [
    {
      "name": "registry",
      "type": "message",
      "description": "registry holds package registry configuration.",
      "message": {
        "name": "DependenciesRegistry",
        "package": "tacplus",
        "description": "DependenciesRegistry holds package registry configuration.",
        "fields": [
          {
            "name": "gitlab_project_id",
            "type": "string",
            "description": "gitlab_project_id is the GitLab project ID for the package registry.",
            "constraints": [
              "maximum size: 32768 bytes (default)"
            ],
            "constraint_infos": [

types.name: EntitlementGrantInfo
types.description:
EntitlementGrantInfo describes one generated entitlement grant token.
 Exact grants name a package + service + RPC. Wildcard grants name a package
 plus a capability scope and expand to the exact grant tokens they cover.

fields.name: token
fields.description:
token is the stable flattened grant token, e.g. PACKAGE_SERVICE_RPC,
 PACKAGE_ANY, or PACKAGE_READ_ANY.

fields.name: package
fields.description: package is the proto package/capability namespace this grant belongs to.

fields.name: service_name
fields.description: service_name is set for exact grants.

fields.name: rpc
fields.description: rpc is set for exact grants.

fields.name: capability_scope
fields.description:
capability_scope is set for wildcard grants: ANY, READ, WRITE, WATCH,
 PAGE, AGENT, or another generated capability scope.

fields.name: expands_to
fields.description:
expands_to lists exact grant tokens implied by a wildcard grant.
 Exact grants leave this empty.

fields.name: routing_alias_packages
fields.description:
routing_alias_packages lists physical routing-alias packages this exact
 grant's (service, rpc) is also reachable under, e.g. an EventBus-hosted
 C2S publish RPC declared in package "tasks" is physically dialed via
 package "eventbus". A token audience-scoped to one of these packages
 should still keep this grant: the alias names the physical dial target,
 not the entitlement contract, which stays this grant's own package.
 Wildcard grants leave this empty.

fields.name: source
fields.description:
source is the layer name (tacplus.yaml `layer` on src / a sources entry) of
 the proto source this grant's package came from, e.g. "platform" or "app".
 Empty when that source declared no layer, the package is built in, or the
 package is declared by files from differently-layered sources. A
 classification input for a consumer's own policy, never an authority.

 tenant's rows or only its own. It is emitted ONLY on the S2S record query
 plane — the synthesized RecordMap service, whose rpcs carry
 (spec.record).s2s_read.auth_services. It is empty everywhere else and says
 nothing about those rpcs.

 surface. "token.namespace" reads as "the caller's namespace is consulted
 uniformly", which here is true only conditionally:

fields.description: enums are the top-level enum definitions in this package.

message.description: EnumInfo describes a top-level protobuf enum definition.

enum_values.name: SMB_ROOT_CLUSTER

fields.description: host_label is the service_s2s label for hosted vservice RPC surfaces.

enum_values.name: RPC_EXPOSURE_EXTERNAL
enum_values.description: RPC_EXPOSURE_EXTERNAL: reachable from outside the cluster boundary.

 matched against the token's `act` claim. Empty means no delegated call is
 admitted at all (see spec.proto's RpcAnnotation.auth_actors).

fields.name: auth_model
fields.description:
auth_model: "s2s" (service-to-service), "c2s" (client-to-service),
 or "c2d" (client-to-daemon local IPC).

fields.name: collection_mode
fields.description:
method_collection (collection-returning read) — see docs/API.md.
 collection_mode is "SNAPSHOT" | "WATCH" | "PAGE"; empty when the RPC is not
 a collection read. The remaining fields are the declared bounds.

fields.name: collection_default_page_size
fields.description:
PAGE keyset default page size when the request omits a limit (0 on
 SNAPSHOT/WATCH). The wrapper bounds an explicit limit to collection_max_items.

fields.name: rpc_verb
fields.description:
Governed RPC classification derived from the method name and streaming /
 collection shape. Empty when the method does not yet classify cleanly.

fields.name: target_namespace_field
fields.description:
Namespace authorization metadata. These fields expose the same level-or-below
 decision inputs that generated authorizers enforce at runtime.

fields.name: verb_status
fields.description: verb_status is "classified", "unclassified", or "exempt".

fields.name: folded_to_verb
fields.description: folded_to_verb is the canonical verb for a rejected leading synonym, when known.

fields.name: surfaces
fields.description:
surfaces lists every generated transport/auth surface for this RPC. This
 includes derived W2S gRPC-over-REST exposure when a C2S RPC has REST route
 metadata.

message.name: RpcSurfaceInfo
message.description: RpcSurfaceInfo describes one transport/auth surface for an RPC.

fields.name: surface_kind
fields.description: surface_kind is "s2s", "c2s", "c2d", or "w2s".

fields.name: transport
fields.description: transport is "grpc", "grpc_over_rest", or "unix".

fields.name: auth_model
fields.description: auth_model is the auth model enforced on this surface.

fields.name: tenant_scope
fields.description:
tenant_scope for this one surface. Non-empty only on the "s2s" surface of
 the record query plane's peer-facing half; see RpcInfo.tenant_scope for the
 values and for why the field exists at all.

fields.name: mcp
fields.description:
mcp is true when the rpc declares principal RPC_PRINCIPAL_MCP: it is an MCP
 tool, not a gRPC call. The tool's description is the `description` field
 (field 8) — the rpc's own doc comment — so there is no second description
 here to drift from it.

fields.name: mcp_tool_name
fields.description:
mcp_tool_name is the tool name this rpc is published under: the RPC name in
 snake_case, or the spec.rpc mcp_tool_name override when one is declared.
 Empty unless mcp is true.

fields.name: mcp_session_carrier
fields.description:
mcp_session_carrier is true for the one rpc per MCP-hosting service that
 tacplus generates rather than the author declaring: the bidirectional
 session over which MCP JSON-RPC frames reach that service's tools. Its
 exposure is the owning ServiceInfo.mcp_exposure. Mutually exclusive with
 `mcp` — the carrier is the transport, not a tool.

fields.name: tenant_scope
fields.description:
tenant_scope says whether an authorized caller of this rpc reads every
 tenant's rows or only its own. It is emitted ONLY on the S2S record query
 plane — the synthesized RecordMap service, whose rpcs carry
 (spec.record).s2s_read.auth_services. It is empty everywhere else and says
 nothing about those rpcs.

 It exists because subject_namespace_source is misleading on this one
 surface. "token.namespace" reads as "the caller's namespace is consulted
 uniformly", which here is true only conditionally:

   "caller_pinned" — consulted, as a RUNTIME branch on the CALLER's own
                     token namespace claim: a /system caller stays
                     fleet-wide, a /tenants/<t> caller reads only <t>'s
                     rows.

 "caller_pinned" is a property of WHO CALLS, not of the record, and not of
 the host. It does NOT depend on the record plane's host declaring
 option (spec.service).tenant_owned: a tenant caller reading through a
 shared host is pinned just the same, which is the entire point of keying
 the boundary on the token rather than on deployment shape. So every rpc on
 this plane carries this one value; there is no second value, because there
 is no longer an S2S record plane generated without the runtime branch.

 No record declares its own tenant scope and no request field selects one —
 a scope a caller could name would not be a tenant boundary. Two callers of
 the same rpc over the same record get different row sets under this value;
 that is what it is reporting.

fields.name: boundaries
fields.description: Boundary names owned by this service's state root.

fields.name: event_label
fields.description: event_label is the routing label for gateway-exposed event services.

fields.name: smb
fields.description:
smb marks a Service Mesh Blackbox service: its own instances talk over a
 black-box peer protocol within a single cluster (SPIFFE
 plan D7). Consumers read this from the registry, not proto text, to drive
 the per-SMB CA + member-cert wiring.

fields.name: smb_authority
fields.description:
smb_authority marks the consumer service designated to issue per-SMB CAs +
 member certs for smb services (SPIFFE plan D7). Read from the registry so an
 SMB service / its tooling can resolve which service to obtain its CA + cert
 from. tacplus does not implement the authority.

fields.name: smb_root
fields.description:
smb_root is present when smb is true and records the trust profile selected
 by spec.smb. SMB_ROOT_ISOLATED is the default; SMB_ROOT_CLUSTER requests a
 per-SMB intermediate rooted in the cluster CA.

enum_values.name: SMB_ROOT_ISOLATED
enum_values.description: SMB_ROOT_ISOLATED uses a self-signed per-SMB CA, scoped only to this SMB.

enum_values.name: SMB_ROOT_CLUSTER
enum_values.description: SMB_ROOT_CLUSTER signs the per-SMB intermediate under the cluster CA.

fields.name: host_label
fields.description: host_label is the service_s2s label for hosted vservice RPC surfaces.

fields.name: mcp
fields.description:
mcp is true when at least one of this service's rpcs declares principal
 RPC_PRINCIPAL_MCP. That fact alone is what decides whether the service gets
 the generated session-carrying MCP transport; it is never declared.

fields.name: mcp_exposure
fields.description:
mcp_exposure is the derived exposure of that generated carrier: the
 most-permissive (union) exposure of this service's MCP rpcs, so one EXTERNAL
 tool makes the carrier reachable from outside to serve it. Meaningless
 unless mcp is true.

enum_values.name: RPC_EXPOSURE_INTERNAL
enum_values.description: RPC_EXPOSURE_INTERNAL: reachable only from inside the cluster boundary.

enum_values.name: RPC_EXPOSURE_EXTERNAL
enum_values.description: RPC_EXPOSURE_EXTERNAL: reachable from outside the cluster boundary.

fields.name: tenant_owned
fields.description:
tenant_owned mirrors (spec.service).tenant_owned: true when the operator
 runs one instance of this service per tenant, identity
 spiffe://<td>/tenants/<tenant>/services/<name>. Read by the operator, the
 gateway, and the record-plane store wrapper. Default false.

fields.name: pinned_tenant
fields.description:
pinned_tenant mirrors (spec.service).pinned_tenant: non-empty when the
 operator runs exactly ONE instance of this tenant-owned service, in that
 tenant, instead of one per configured tenant. Meaningful only when
 tenant_owned is true. Read by the operator. Default empty.

fields.name: volume_groups
fields.description:
volume_groups mirrors this service's (spec.volume_group) declarations: the
 blob-store volume groups it owns. Read by the operator to render the blob
 store's group config. Group names are unique fleet-wide.

fields.name: max_blob_bytes

fields.name: tenant_quota_bytes

fields.name: source
fields.description:
source is the layer name (tacplus.yaml `layer` on src / a sources entry) of
 the proto source this service's file came from, e.g. "platform" or "app".
 Empty when that source declared no layer or the service is built in.
 A classification input for a consumer's own policy, never an authority.

TransformationInfo describes a derived row type produced by a pure typed
 conversion of a source message. Store-neutral: dedup and cardinality_hint are
 semantic intent, not backend DDL. It carries no lifetime: a pure typed
 conversion has none.

message.name: TransformationFieldInfo

projection source path from (spec.projection_source), e.g. "agent_id" or "tool_use.tool_name".

fields.name: timeseries_partition_key

fields.name: store_key

 or multiple_of for compound numeric annotations.

fields.name: defaulted

fields.name: unit

fields.name: source

fields.name: timeseries_cardinality_hint
fields.description:
Store-neutral distinct-value hint from (spec.timeseries_column).cardinality_hint.
 (Field 25, the spec's suggested number, is already taken by `oneof`.)

fields.name: data_entitlement_mode
fields.description:
data-entitlement mode for this field, from (spec.redact) or inherited from the
 message-level (spec.data_entitlement) default: DROP / PSEUDONYMIZE /
 MAY_REDACT / MAY_ANONYMIZE. UNSPECIFIED = not annotated (never transformed).
 This field's wire number is the field id reported in the sanitize
 redacted-id set and checked by the data-entitlement drift guard.

fields.name: filter_mode
fields.description:
filter_mode is the field's RecordMap filterability, from (spec.query_field).op:
 EQ  -> the generated <T>Filter carries `optional <type> <name>`;
 RANGE -> it carries `optional <type> <name>_from` + `optional <type> <name>_to`.
 UNSPECIFIED = the field carries no (spec.query_field) and is NOT filterable — a
 record type whose fields are all UNSPECIFIED gets no <T>Filter message at all.

fields.name: store_principal
fields.description:
Store-boundary role markers, so a registry consumer names a field by its
 ANNOTATION rather than by matching the field's spelling. A service whose
 principal field is not literally "recipient" is invisible to a name-matching
 heuristic, and a boundary that depends on spelling is not a boundary.
 True when this field carries (spec.store_principal).

fields.description: True when this field carries (spec.store_namespace).

message.name: TransformationInfo

 semantic intent, not backend DDL. It carries no lifetime: a pure typed
 conversion has none.

rpcs.description:
ManageCert: bidi cert lifecycle. Any authenticated service may open a
 stream — the SecurityInterceptor validates the bearer token before
 the handler runs, and the handler matches the token's location-agnostic
 service path (token.service_path(), derived from sub_type/sub — never a
 raw SPIFFE URI claim) to the requested service_name in the first Init
 message.

services.name: TlsCertService
services.description:
TlsCertService provides automatic TLS certificate lifecycle management.
 The certificate authority service implements the server side. Services with
 auto_tls: true open a bidi stream via the generated ServiceManager.

 Flow:
   1. Service sends Init (identifies itself) + Csr (public key)
   2. Certificate authority signs cert under service's intermediate CA, returns CertDelivery
   3. At half-life, certificate authority sends Renew
   4. Service generates new keypair, sends Csr
   5. Certificate authority signs, returns CertDelivery
   6. Repeat from 3

types.name: TokenRequestParams
types.description:
TokenRequestParams contains parameters for token requests.
 These map to URL parameters used in token endpoint requests.

 The generate_from_map option instructs the compiler to generate a FromMap method
 that converts a map[string]string (URL parameters) to this message type.
 - key_enum: Specifies which enum to use for validating parameter keys (TokenParamKey)

values.name: JWT_PAYLOAD_TYPE_NAMESPACE
values.description:
--- Namespace (authorization scope) ---
 `namespace` is the caller's authorization-tree scope, e.g. "/" (root),
 "/system/...", "/tenants/acme", or "/tenants/acme/workspaces/dev". It is
 an authorization fact, NOT the subject identity. The subject SPIFFE ID is
 a COMPUTATION over the structured claims (sub_type, sub, namespace,
 service_name) performed by the generated sys/spiffe helper
 (token.subject_spiffe_id); it is never carried as a wire claim. The
 universal level-or-below rule (target_namespace_field) compares namespace
 paths directly via the path-segment-aware is_at_or_below relation.

enums.description: GrantType represents OAuth 2.0 grant types

enums.description: TokenPurpose distinguishes the purpose of a token in minting requests.

values.name: TOKEN_PURPOSE_REFRESH
values.description: Refresh token — long-lived, used to obtain new access tokens.

values.name: TOKEN_PURPOSE_ACCESS
values.description: Access token — short-lived, carries entitlements for a specific service.

values.name: TOKEN_PURPOSE_SERVICE
values.description: Service token — access token scoped to a specific target service (aud).

values.name: TOKEN_PURPOSE_BOOTSTRAP
values.description:
Bootstrap token — very short-lived, used to bootstrap a child workload.
 Parent mints this via WorkloadMint and passes it to the child process.
 Child exchanges it with the token authority for a real access + refresh pair.

values.name: TOKEN_PURPOSE_LOCALITY
values.description:
Locality token — rotated by parent, shared with all children.
 Children present this on refresh to prove they can still reach their parent.

enums.name: TokenUse
enums.description: TokenUse claim values — identifies the purpose of a token in the token_use claim.

values.name: TOKEN_USE_EXTERNAL
values.description:
TOKEN_USE_EXTERNAL marks a token minted by the token authority for use with an external upstream service.
 Internal service auth middleware rejects any token carrying this token_use value,
 preventing a compromised proxy from replaying an externally-minted credential
 against platform-internal services.

values.name: TOKEN_USE_OFFLINE
values.description:
TOKEN_USE_OFFLINE is the long-lived, identity-only Offline Token (OT) held
 by the client daemon on disk. Carries no entitlements (its long TTL would
 make an embedded entitlement snapshot lie). Used as input to mint AT, and to
 self-renew via TokenMint(input=OT, no aud).

enums.description: SubType claim values — identifies what the token subject represents.

enums.description: TokenType represents the type of authentication token

Config configures the JWT token cache used for authentication.
 Controls how tokens and JWK signing keys are cached and refreshed.

fields.description:
dynamic_lookup enables automatic JWK fetching from OIDC endpoints.
 When true, JWKs are automatically fetched from token issuer's
 .well-known/openid-configuration endpoint.
 When false, only manually added static keys are used.
 Default: true

lifetime_seconds is how long before cached JWK keys are refreshed.
 Default: 604800 (1 week)

fields.name: expire_unused_seconds
fields.description:
expire_unused_seconds is how long before unused JWK keys are evicted.
 Default: 86400 (24 hours)

fields.name: refresh_interval_seconds
fields.description:
refresh_interval_seconds is how often the cleanup goroutine runs.
 Default: 3600 (1 hour)
